result.summary:
KEEP, severity minor. I could not refute the candidate on determinism or safety grounds. The fast path is a serial rewrite of sell_top_ups (native_executor.rs:9858-9916) on the exec thread. It visits the same candidates in the same global flat order and does the same arithmetic. It touches no consensus code, and the fault and panic paths stay fail-stop. Two details the candidate leaves implicit would break byte-identity if missed:
(1) The stitch record must store the basis-overridden reservation quantity, not params.quantity. Market and IOC/FOK sells are top-up candidates and do get basis overrides.
(2) The per-sender run cache may call bal_cache.set only when the run made at least one grant, and it must also write back after the last run. A set without a grant turns a clean entry dirty. That causes an extra CF_NATIVE_BALANCES put, and that CF is in the running hash (id 2).
The bench cannot prove byte-identity: every node runs the same arm, so AGREE only checks that flag-on nodes agree with each other, not with main. Main's 300m shape also never exercises the partial or none grant paths, or basis overrides. Differential tests are therefore the only guard and must come before any A/B. Part (b), the s92 counter loop, only feeds telemetry. Part (c), the MatchRequest change, is out of scope here.

result.constraints:
1. ORDER: record candidates only in stitch_outcome's Pass arm, in both stitch loops (sharded 7505-7527, serial 7533-7560). Both iterate place_order_indices, which is built strictly ascending (7260-7315, also on the TORUS_CANCEL_BATCH path); the cloid retain (7340) keeps the order. In debug builds, assert that the list is strictly ascending by flat index and that its length equals the number of top_up_candidate PreparedOrders. This catches any future PreparedOrder that does not come through stitch.
2. RECORD FIELDS: (flat index i, market, k = the market Vec's len before the push, sender, reserved = pass.required, res_qty). res_qty must be basis.get(&i).map_or(params.quantity, |b| b.1), or prepare_one's own res_qty carried in PrepPass (7980-7983). takes_bid_floor (9470) includes Market and IOC/FOK sells, and phase2_reservation_basis (9589-9674) overrides their price and quantity.
3. SAME PER-CANDIDATE SEMANTICS, IN TODAY'S ORDER:
   - market missing: skip.
   - Top-up price None (sell_top_up_price, which may be cached per market because it is pure): skip.
   - try_reserve_for_qty_cfg error: skip.
   - extra = target - reserved <= 0: skip, with no load.
   - Load error: note_reader_fault with the same label "sell top-up balance read"; no cache insert; skip; the next candidate retries the load.
   - grant = extra.min(bal.available + pos_net - excess), evaluated per candidate on the updated bal.available. Do not fold this into a running "free" value: FixedPoint +/- panic on overflow (torus-types lib.rs:235-268).
   - grant <= 0: none++.
   - Otherwise, per grant: bal.available -= grant; bal.order_margin += grant; margin_reserved = reserved + grant; on a full grant, res_price = price; increment the counts as today.
4. LAZY LOAD: load the sender's balance only at the first candidate of a run with extra > 0, which are today's load points. Then the cache key set and the fault sites stay the same.
5. WRITE-BACK: call bal_cache.set once per run, only if the run made at least one grant > 0. Do it when the sender changes and after the last candidate, before d2_pools (7595). Use BalanceCache::set, or copy its dirty flag and dirty-list push exactly; never mutate map entries without that bookkeeping. A spurious set adds a CF_NATIVE_BALANCES put, and that CF is hashed (running_hash.rs HASHED_CFS id 2).
6. Finish all PreparedOrder writes (in the loop or in a deferred pass) before Phase 3 reads market_batches (7616). If r1-match-core-1 also lands, these writes must happen before its match jobs are dispatched.
7. NO NEW PANICS: use get_mut + continue as at 9881, or debug_assert; no direct indexing. An exec panic is a fail-stop (app.rs:4623-4629), so a deterministic panic on every flag-on node halts a 3/3 fleet.
8. PER-CALL LIST: use a local Vec, or ctx scratch cleared at the START of each execute_batch call. There are two calls per block (app.rs:3738-3739) and early returns at 7371 and 7754.
9. FLAG: with the flag unset, record nothing (pass None into stitch), so the control arm runs main's code. Read the flag once (OnceLock), accept =1 only, and log the resolved value. Add a ctx or test override in the style of EngineMode::Force / test_flush_per_row, because the integration tests share one process.
10. TESTS FIRST; the bench cannot catch a divergence from main:
   - Differential execute_batch, flag on vs off, on Batch, Parallel and the worker-panic fallback. Compare results, the CF dump plus state root and running hash, PreparedOrder fields, BalanceCache rows with dirty flags (template native_executor.rs:13447-13455), and the counters.
   - Fuzz cases: senders A,B,A with partial grants spanning two runs; a run whose first candidate has extra <= 0; runs with only none outcomes; a last run that has grants; Market sells and IOC/FOK sells with a closing allowance; a market without a bid; price or notional overflow; an injected balance-read fault (same label, empty cache rows).
   - Run these with the flag forced on: account_margin_tests (partial_top_up_goes_in_flat_order, top_up_never_rejects_a_placement and the other batch_paths), engine_parallel_tests, perf_equivalence_golden and the r02 top-up tests. Add an assertion that the goldens hit partial and none (today they only print the counts).
   - Optional: one mixed-flag devnet cell (one node on, two off), so AGREE checks byte-identity at node level.
11. Keep "sell_top_ups" in the new function's name: storage_reads_tests.rs:79 classifies storage reads by frame name.
12. Phase 5 step 2 removes BalanceCache. If the A/B wins, make the fast path the only path before step 2 starts; if it loses, drop it. Either way only one variant gets ported.
13. Part (b), the s92 counter loop, is telemetry only (record_margin_cuts: "nothing reads it back"); only the counter totals must stay the same. Part (c) (MatchRequest / taker_margin_limit) is not part of this candidate.
result.verified:
- Order is unchanged. place_order_indices is strictly ascending: the plain loop and the TORUS_CANCEL_BATCH loop both push in increasing i (native_executor.rs:7260-7315), and the cloid retain keeps order (7340). Both stitch loops walk it (7508, 7533), so recording at stitch gives exactly today's sort_unstable_by_key on the unique flat index (9871-9877).
- market_batches is local to each call (7379). Only stitch_outcome pushes PreparedOrders in production code (8205-8218; the only other constructions are in tests). Nothing mutates market_batches between the stitch and sell_top_ups (7563-7588), so recorded k, reserved and sender equal what sell_top_ups reads today.
- pools and excess_by_sender are read-only and keyed by sender, so caching them per run is exact. markets is immutable, so a per-market top-up price is exact.
- BalanceCache::set pushes to the dirty list only when an entry first becomes dirty (367-386), and flush_all sorts that list (403). One set per run therefore gives the same values and the same dirty set as several sets.
- The Phase-2 fold always loads a candidate's sender (checked orders load at 8020-8021) and marks it dirty when required > 0 (8123-8127). A clean entry is still reachable in edge cases, hence constraint 5.
- CF_NATIVE_BALANCES is hashed in the running hash (crates/torus-state/src/running_hash.rs:35-63, id 2), which folds every block's logical write set.
- Balance-read errors are always local faults: State from get_cf_raw, Borsh from decode_native_balance (torus-core position.rs:282-283, 379-408; error.rs:164-173). note_reader_fault records them, and the committer's take_fatal_error (native_executor.rs:5325; app.rs:3747) fail-stops before any flush. So what happens after a fault never reaches committed state.
- Exec-thread panics are caught and latch exec_failed (app.rs:4623-4629).
- No consensus, persistence or format change; restart and replay are unaffected, and the flag can be flipped across a restart.
- In-code precedent for a run cache: SenderFold::state's cur slot (2269-2280), tested by projections_tests.
- Main metrics, hsdb-300m-r2-B val1: sell_top_ups_full_total 91,156,649, partial 0, none 0, maker_margin_cancels 0, reduce_only_cuts 0, 2,051 native blocks.
- Profile shares as stated: 5.74% and 5.46% of exec samples.
- No ref implements this: git grep over all branches for FAST_SELL_TOP_UPS / sell_top_ups_fast finds nothing.
result.refuted:
No determinism claim is refuted. Corrections and gaps:
(a) The record "(flat index, market, k, sender, quantity, reserved)" is ambiguous. quantity must be the basis-overridden res_qty. The test plan's "reduce-only" basis case does not apply, because reduce-only orders are not match-checked and so are never candidates. The relevant basis cases are Market sells (mark-price basis) and Market/IOC/FOK sells with a closing allowance.
(b) "Written back with bal_cache.set when the sender changes" is unsafe as written. The set must happen only if the run made a grant, and also after the last run.
(c) "Senders' balances ... disjoint, so the order across senders never mattered" is true but does not matter here: the fast path keeps the global flat order anyway.
(d) The bench plan cannot validate determinism. With 3/3 nodes on the same arm, AGREE only compares flag-on nodes with each other. Main's 300m shape has 0 partial and 0 none top-ups and only GTC limit sells, so the running-balance and basis paths are never exercised there.
(e) The merged duplicate's claim that "the counters it feeds stay 0" holds for maker_margin_cancels and reduce_only_cuts (verified 0). sell_margin_cuts is not covered by that check, which does not matter because it is telemetry only.

result.constraints:
Implementation:
1. Use a per-call toggle: a ctx field, or an execute_batch_*_mode entry like execute_batch_cancel_mode or EngineMode::Force. A OnceLock env read cannot be flipped for in-process flag-off vs flag-on differential tests. With this plumbing the size is about 150-250 lines plus tests, not 80-120.
2. Carry res_qty in PrepPass, using exactly prepare_one's basis rule (basis.get(&i), else params.quantity). The stored reserved must equal pass.required.
3. Push to a per-call list or a drained scratch Vec. execute_batch runs twice per block (pre- and post-EVM), and only one stitch path runs per call; the worker-panic fallback to the serial loop is fine.
4. Write the run cache back with bal_cache.set only when the run granted at least once. An unconditional set adds a dirty entry, so flush_all makes an extra put_native_balance, and the write set and h_n then differ from flag off.
5. Load lazily, only when extra > 0, so the cache key set stays the same.
6. A sender can have several non-adjacent runs in one block (MAX_IN_FLIGHT=4), so write back at every sender change.
7. Keep the per-candidate skip and the exact fault text "sell top-up balance read". The r02_sell_top_up_* tests call sell_top_ups directly with a hand-built market_batches, so the fast path needs a test entry that builds the list.

result.constraints:
1. **Source of the vector.** Build the aligned Vec<Option<Address>> in the SAME pool read-lock pass as verified_restash_keys (crates/torus-mempool/src/native_pool.rs:357-369). Use the hashes dispatch_to_exec already computes over torus_block.native_actions in body order (crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:8009-8013). An index is Some(entry.sender) only if entry.restash_key.is_some(). Do no second hashing and never take a sender from an entry whose restash_key is None. Keep the existing cache_verified_sender restash unchanged, so fallback and gossip T2.1 behave as today.
2. **Mask in eip712 itself.** Use carried[i] only when actions[i].signature is ActionSignature::Eip712. Today's batch_verify_impl would keep a carried Some on a session action: recover_one returns *hit for any Some (crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:1145-1153), and phase 2's `_ => {}` (1320-1338) leaves it in place when the session is missing, expired or out of scope, or the action requires EIP-712. That is a fork.
3. **Bind the vector to its block.**
   - Put it inside the CommittedBlockMsg built in the same dispatch_to_exec call.
   - For rank-2 Full-park retries (exec_prepared_height gate at app.rs:7964; compact put-back re-materializes the block), store it beside exec_prepared_durable with (height, block hash). Reuse it only if both match; otherwise send None.
   - At exec, if carried.len() != native_actions.len(), ignore the whole vector, count it and warn. Never index-panic on the exec thread.
4. **Gate.** Gate on the env flag AND ExecutionContext.exec_trust_cache (app.rs:960, read at 3394). With the trust cache off, carried senders are ignored.
5. **Flag unset = main.** The original remove_committed_native and batch_verify_native_actions_cached paths run unchanged, no aligned vector is built and the field is None. The phase-1 skip sits behind a flag too.
6. **Phase-1 skip predicate.** Return cache_hits unchanged only if every action is either Session or has cache_hits[i].is_some(). The behavior must be identical under the Serial, Default and Pool(n) VerifyModes.
7. **Replay and recovery pass None.** This covers boot replay (execute_committed_block, app.rs:2212-2218 and 6188), the F-1 manifest re-park, block-sync and tests. Do not change the identity of verified_cache_key or compute_action_hash, and add no consensus-thread hashing.
8. **Observability.**
   - Add counters for exec carried hits, fallbacks and length-mismatch ignores, and keep the exec_verify timer around the new call.
   - With the flag on, torus_verified_sender_cache_hits drops by about 707k per run because the exec lookups disappear, so the exec-miss inference no longer works.
   - Skipping phase 1 may leave the global rayon pool uninitialized. The 32 'torus-execution' namesake threads then move or disappear in io-threads.
9. **Tests before any A/B.**
   - (a) eip712 differential: carried-variant output equals batch_verify_native_actions with a cold cache and the cached variant with a warm cache, in every VerifyMode. Fixtures: tampered signature, tampered body, session valid / expired / out of scope / requires-EIP-712 / unregistered, duplicates, carried Some on a session action (must be ignored), wrong-length vector (must be ignored).
   - (b) mempool property test: across add_native_action, add_native_action_presigned (EIP-712 and session), add_native_action_from_gossip (with and without a T2.1 hit) and the trusted path, carried is Some iff the action is EIP-712 and locally verified, and the sender equals recover_sender().
   - (c) consensus test modeled on trust_cache_resolved_senders_identical_cached_vs_uncached (app.rs:13535), extended through dispatch to exec: pooled, unpooled and rank-2-parked blocks (TORUS_EXEC_NONBLOCKING_DISPATCH=1 with a full channel) all reach a state digest equal to a cold node.
   - (d) one untimed shadow cell in which exec also computes key + lookup / recover for carried actions and counts mismatches. It must be 0.
   - AGREE in every cell.
10. **Coordinate with 18c.** exp/s123-exec-action-keys-parallel edits the same batch_verify_impl. Run separate arms. If both flags are ever stacked, the parallel key pre-pass must cover only non-carried actions.

I could not refute this on determinism or safety grounds. Both parts change only who runs the exec-pool jobs, not what those jobs compute:
- K x cap chunks: reuses run_jobs unchanged.
- Caller runner: lets torus-execution take jobs itself.

Why the output stays byte-identical:
- Match: the results are sorted by market id right after the call (native_executor.rs:7771). Nothing reads them before the sort.
- Pass A: plans go back by input index (8705-8713), and the fallback and fault are picked in index order (8725-8766).
- Each market's work touches only its own book or its own fresh PositionCache. The only shared state is read-only: a frozen backend, the memo of OnceLock cells (poison-tolerant), and the fault OnceLock, whose message is node-local and fatal anyway.
- The per-thread MAKER_FREE cache is keyed by a BatchSums id that is never reused (1446-1468, 1478-1485). The backend is frozen from 7436 until the cache flush (7859-7881), and every reader built after the flush uses batch: None (10324-10335). So the cache is also safe on the exec thread.
- Existing tests already prove that changing the cap changes nothing, including cap above the market count, which gives one market per chunk: parallel_settle_tests.rs:376 and :394.

Running these jobs on torus-execution is not new:
- Match already runs inline when only one market has orders (market_workers.rs:127-133). It uses plain catch_unwind, so a panic there hits the R01b hook and exits 70.
- Pass A already runs inline when there is at most one chunk (native_executor.rs:8675-8677). plan_for wraps it in catch_recoverable (8648-8660), so the hook skips it and the sequential fallback runs.

No consensus code, persistence or flag-unset path changes. Every node gets the same state whatever K or caller setting it uses, so a mixed fleet is safe.

The candidate needs these corrections, all fixable:
- Its test-plan item "a job panic on torus-execution does not trip the hook" holds only for pass A. A match panic must stay fatal for the block.
- Applying the grain when the cap is 1 would break the "cap 1 = serial" contract.
- K x cap needs overflow and env handling.
- The caller mode must be a new, safe-Rust runner, not a change to run_jobs.

Coordination: origin/exp/s123-parallel-cancel-all-book-pass is still at 73c99111 ("compile fixes in progress (not yet building or tested)"). It uses chunk_indices, run_jobs and run_contained and returns results per market, so it can take the grain flag once it builds.

result.summary:
Keep. I could not refute it on determinism or safety.

- The hold only changes when a leader proposes. Validation has no timing or payload-count rule, so different flag values across nodes cannot fork, and every node keeps identical state for the same blocks.
- The deferral path it reuses already exists on main (`proposal_deferred` plus the 10 ms re-poll, capped by the view deadline). A view change clears the deferral, so a leader cannot propose for a view it has left.
- With D=0 the code can be made identical to main.
- The mechanism shows up in a log: the idle chain in hsdb-300m-r2-B val0 has 14 commit gaps of 1.208-1.215 s, one every 26-28 heights. That fits the per-author bucket of 50 tokens running out at about 2 messages per author per view.

Two gaps in the candidate as written:
1. Its claim that "TC and recovery proposals are never held" does not follow from the hook site. After a timeout certificate (TC), `create_proposal_based_on_tc` returns None in two cases: when the highest QC wins, and when the leader lacks the winning tip block and starts RECOVER. `enter_view` then falls through to the fresh-proposal path, where the hold would sit. Leader-skip entries also go through that path. A held proposal racing the RECOVER handlers would give two proposals in one view, which followers record as equivocation. Explicit guards fix this.
2. The optional rate-limit knob needs a floor: a value of 0 drops every consensus gossip message and halts the chain.

Preferred variant: a minimum spacing between proposals that ignores payload size, i.e. hold until the previous view's entry time plus D. It automatically excludes the TC, skip and recovery views. It never delays the commit of a full block, needs no App hook (so no mempool locks on the consensus thread), and never binds at 300m or at 10m depth 4.

Side finding, pre-existing on main, from reading the code only (not seen live): in the RECOVER case main already proposes twice in one view. The fresh proposal goes out from the fall-through, then `on_receive_proposal_response` (implementation.rs:1977) or `on_receive_ne` (:2136) proposes again. No test covers this; worth sending to 18c.

The required guards exclude only views after a timeout, skip-entered views and recovery views. Those follow long views and are not the fast runs that drain the bucket, so they cost none of the gain. result.summary: KEEP, severity minor. I found nothing in the determinism or safety lens that cannot be made safe. The change is a RocksDB storage-layout option on one node-local CF, cf_native_pending in the consensus DB, and that CF is unhashed, never deleted and only point-read. Reads return the same bytes in both layouts, so the flag cannot change state, the state hash, AGREE or what consensus decides. Integrated BlobDB in the bundled RocksDB 10.4.2 is crash-safe for this use: blob files are fsynced before the MANIFEST edit, stray blob files are removed at open, and blob references stay readable with the flag off and in read-only opens. Turning the flag on or off on an existing data dir is safe both ways. The real risks are liveness, latency and operations, and the candidate understated three of them. (1) Consensus-thread DA reads (follower validate reconstruct, leader missing()) often hit flushed data, not the memtable: pool residency p50 is about 5-6 s against about 7.5 s of DA writes per 128 MiB memtable. With ZSTD blobs, each such read decompresses ZSTD where today's L0/L5 data is LZ4. Expect a few ms per view, so these timers must be guarded. (2) Blob compression moves into flush, and flush runs on the single rocksdb:high thread shared by the state DB and the consensus DB. (3) With blob GC off, blob files grow by one per flush (about 116 per node per 600 s at 300m). Overwritten duplicates (18% of flushed keys) stay on disk as garbage, so file count and disk grow faster than today. That is fine for 600 s A/B cells but not for default-on before DA retention and blob GC exist. Skip the optional cf_block_bodies arm.

KEEP, minor. Nothing earlier splits exec-pool work into finer jobs or lets the exec thread take items: I found no such proposal in memory, git (all refs), docs/perf, docs/plans, the s64/s65 explorer files or the s123 lens. result.refuted:
1. "A phase ends only when the latest starter finishes" is only half true. Per match phase, the last 3 finishers start late (start rank ~0.8), but 84-87% of them were also descheduled mid-chunk: median ~8 ms of gaps over 3 ms between samples (pass A: 72-74%, ~4.5 ms). Rayon cannot steal a job that is already running, so finer chunks recover only part of that tail.
2. The candidate's rate model roughly doubles what a replay on the observed CPU windows gives. The model (sum r_i*(T-s_i)=W, span x0.6) gives -7.1..-7.3 ms per match phase at the median (mean -9.3..-9.8) and -4.7..-5.2 ms per pass A phase. My replay, which keeps the observed mid-chunk gaps, gives:
   - K=4, optimistic: match -3.3..-3.5 ms median (-4.3..-4.9 mean); pass A -2.0..-2.2 (-2.5..-2.8).
   - K=4, pessimistic (threads that keep working are descheduled on the observed duty cycle): match -1.9 (-2.6..-3.3); pass A -0.6..-0.7 (-1.1..-1.3).
   - K=8 adds at most 0.5 ms.
   - Scripts are in /tmp/advcheck-grain.
3. "Match pool part about 27 ms" is wrong. phase_match = 31.37 ms (checked in hsdb-300m-r2-B summary.json) includes ~10-11 ms of serial setup at native_executor.rs:7612-7714 (memories cc05dbcb and ea9b3f0d), so the pool part is ~20-21 ms.
4. The caller flag does not remove "most of the end wake-up". ThreadPool::in_place_scope called from a non-worker thread waits on CountLatchKind::Blocking, a mutex+condvar LockLatch (rayon-core-1.13.0 scope/mod.rs:667-675, latch.rs:386-399), until every spawned helper has run, including helpers that find no items. Only the start-side saving and the exec thread's own work are real: about 0.4-0.7 ms per phase in the replay. Raw handoffs are exec to pool 1.5-1.8 ms and pool to exec 2.1-2.5 ms, of which ~1-2 ms is sampling bias.
5. The panic risk is overstated:
   - Pass A plan_for already wraps each market in catch_recoverable (native_executor.rs:8648-8660; the comment there says it already runs on torus-execution when there is one chunk).
   - A match panic is fatal either way (panic_scope.rs:8-10).
   - The single-market fast path already runs match on torus-execution (market_workers.rs:127-133).
   - No new panic handling is needed, only tests.
6. The acceptance rule "match ms down >= 15%" is set wrong. 15% of 31.4 ms is 4.7 ms, which is above even the optimistic pool-part saving (~4 ms).

result.summary:
Not refuted. Step 1 sets TORUS_HASH_ONLY_PUSH_THRESHOLD=512000, the compiled production default, instead of the bench's 8000000 pin. That only changes how bodies travel to followers, and it cannot make nodes disagree on state:
- Receivers accept both the 0xFD body batch and the 0xFC hash manifest, whatever the proposer chose (crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:1661-1704).
- The proposer writes every referenced body to its own DA store before the bundle is sent (crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:7130-7134, then 7188-7198).
- Bodies are content-addressed. compute_action_hash covers the canonical bytes, the nonce and the tagged signature (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1183-1216). A pulled body is stored under a hash recomputed from it (crates/torus-state/src/native_da.rs:97-123; app.rs:6475-6491).
- A follower votes only once it holds the body (hotstuff implementation.rs:2646-2709; app.rs:7022-7090). A missing body costs vote delay or a timeout, never a fork.

The archive has a natural experiment. The ozarchy-p3cloid-300m c100 cells sent about half their pushes as manifests; the c0 cells sent almost none:
- Followers pulled bodies on 5-19% of manifest receipts, about 0.7-0.9% of body checks. The largest single pull was 232 bodies.
- Hot-path MissingData was 0-2 per node per cell, against 0-1 in c0.
- view_vote_delay did not move (20-27 vs 22-28 ms).
- Timeouts were 8.5 vs 6.75 per cell. That gap is not resolved and is confounded by the cloid load.

Two risks are open:
- **Crash and rejoin were never run with manifests on this bench.** T4 re-push keeps only full-body bundles, and the off-loop DA serve answers requests beyond 8 in flight with empty bodies.
- **Optional step 2 and the merged early-dedup plan touch two invariants that keep nodes in agreement:** each DA key must equal the hash of the body stored under it, and native_hashes must stay in step with the block's action list.
result.corrected_gain:

- **Device writes:** about -10 to -14 MB/s per node.
- **matched/s:** 0 to +0.3%. This cannot be resolved because 300m is exec-bound.
- **Steady-state liveness cost:** pre-warm pulls on 5-19% of follower manifest receipts and about +1 hot-path MissingData per node per 120 s, with no measurable change in vote delay.

1. "Order age at commit <0.32 s for 0.68%" does not bound how often followers lack a body. Age at the Commit stage already includes 2-3 views. Non-cancel selection runs in (sender address, nonce) order (native_pool.rs:46), which favours fresh actions from low-address senders. Measured instead: 5-19% of manifest receipts trigger a pull, up to 232 bodies at once.
2. Pulls do not always land in the pre-warm window. plan_prewarm_requests checks presence in RocksDB only (native_da.rs:261-263), so bodies sitting in the follower's own da_pending buffer are pulled needlessly. Pulls over 128 bodies exceed the 8-slot serve pool, which answers the excess empty (swarm.rs:613, 1990-2006), and those views fall back to MissingData and the recovery worker.
3. The risk 'manifests are not retained for T4' is understated:
   - T4 re-push keeps only full-body bundles (swarm.rs:2718-2729, 2247-2271).

4. The merged plan's 'put_batch with precomputed hashes' is not a neutral refactor. Reconstruct uses the DA key without re-hashing the body, so a key not derived from the stored bytes would make nodes execute different bodies for the same compact hash.
5. Step 2a's 'skip the deep clone' is only possible on the manifest path. The clone becomes the block body, and native_hashes ordering is load-bearing for the compact block.

result.summary:
KEEP, minor. Under the determinism and safety lens this is safe. It changes only how the RPC formats its reply: the handler runs on the dedicated 4-worker rpc-worker runtime (crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:1219-1242), reads owned bytes with no lock shared with exec, writes nothing, and touches no consensus, exec, state, mempool or DA code. Nothing in the node calls get_block_body; its users are the bench tail, the bench sweep, the explorer, devnet scripts and the r01-fault diagnostics.

Byte-identity, checked:
- serde_json 1.0.149 is the only copy in Cargo.lock. raw_value is on; arbitrary_precision is off.
- preserve_order is on, but only indirectly: revm 36's default 'tracer' feature enables revm-inspector's serde_json dependency, which carries preserve_order.
- NativeAction and every type inside it has no flatten, no maps and no floats.
- So with the flag on, the output equals main whenever every integer fits in 64 bits.
- One real difference: an i128/u128 outside the u64/i64 range. Main's Value serializer fails there (NumberOutOfRange), and unwrap_or_default prints null for the whole action. The raw path prints the digits. This is reachable, because ingress does not range-check prices, quantities or order ids. It is benign and arguably a fix.

Nothing fatal or major. The risks are all in how it is built:
- Hand-built raw JSON would panic the rpc-worker, because jsonrpsee re-parses the whole reply with expect(). The panic line fails AGREE.
- Using the global rayon pool would bring back the s352 starvation.
- A test that compares Values cannot catch key-order drift, because serde_json Map equality ignores order.
- Each action must still fall back to null on its own, so indices stay aligned with nativeActionStatus.
result.constraints:
1. SCOPE. Change only the native_actions mapping in get_block_body (crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1800-1804).
   - Keep the read order: body at 1790, then the applied height at 1815, then the status record at 1817. The comment at 1808-1812 explains why the applied height must be read first.
   - Serialize only from the owned decoded body. Hold no lock or RocksDB snapshot while serializing.
   - Leave every other RPC method, stream, consensus, exec, state, mempool and DA path alone.

2. FLAG. Off by default.
   - Parse it with a pure function from the raw env string, like resolve_max_response_bytes (crates/torus-rpc/src/lib.rs:67).
   - Read it once when the server is built and keep it in RpcState: not per request, and no std::env::set_var in tests.
   - With the flag unset, the existing `serde_json::to_value(a).unwrap_or_default()` code must run unchanged.
   - Pick one name; the two drafts disagree (TORUS_RPC_BODY_RAW_JSON vs TORUS_RPC_RAW_BODY). Keep the TORUS_ prefix so run-cell.sh clears it between cells and records it in NODE_ENV_JSON.

3. HOW EACH ITEM IS BUILT.
   - Use only serde_json::value::to_raw_value(a).
   - On Err, push RawValue::NULL.to_owned(), so there is exactly one entry per action, aligned with nativeActionStatus and nativeActionFailures.
   - Never skip an action, never turn a failure into an RPC error, and no unwrap or expect.
   - Never hand-build JSON text or call RawValue::from_string. jsonrpsee-core 0.26 method_response.rs:190-193 re-parses the whole reply with `RawValue::from_string(..).expect(..)`, so invalid embedded JSON panics the rpc-worker. rpc-worker is not a fail-stop thread (main.rs:2166-2213), but the panic line fails AGREE.
   - Do not stream actions straight into the response writer: a failure halfway through one action cannot be undone, so the per-action null fallback would be lost.

4. CONCURRENCY. Keep the loop serial inside the rpc-worker task.
   - No rayon par_iter: the global pool runs exec-thread batch_verify_native_actions (VerifyMode::Default) and per-market matching. The s352 starvation is documented at torus.rs:561-569.
   - No ingress_verify_pool, no new pool, no spawn_blocking changes.

5. TESTS FIRST, AND THEY MUST COMPARE BYTES.
   - Compare serde_json::to_string of the flag-off and flag-on responses, or the raw HTTP reply text.
   - Never compare Value == Value: serde_json Map equality is IndexMap equality, which ignores order (serde_json map.rs:409-413; indexmap map.rs:1876-1883). The existing test at lib.rs:3612-3686 compares Values and would miss key-order drift.
   - Cover every NativeAction variant:
     - PlaceOrder and PlaceOrderBatch, each with and without a cloid, including StopMarket and StopLimit;
     - CancelOrder, CancelAllOrders with Some and None, CancelByCloid, ModifyOrder;
     - the U256 and Address variants, SubmitOraclePrices (a Vec of tuples), CreateSession;
     - AttestStateHash, SetOracleSigner with and without a proof;
     - Session (Ed25519Sig) and EIP-712 signatures;
     - legacy JSON and BinV1 records;
     - executed, not-yet-executed and empty bodies.
   - This byte test also guards preserve_order, which comes only from revm 36's default 'tracer' feature through revm-inspector. If that feature goes away, flag-off output switches to sorted keys while flag-on keeps declaration order.

6. DOCUMENT AND TEST THE ONE INTENDED DIFFERENCE.
   - Affected values: a FixedPoint raw value below i64::MIN or above u64::MAX, and an order_id of 2^64 or more.
   - Flag off (= main) prints null for the whole action (serde_json 1.0.149 value/ser.rs:96-146). Flag on prints the digits.
   - It is reachable: ingress does not range-check these; validate_order_price runs only at exec (native_executor.rs:9574).
   - Cloids are not affected: they serialize as hex strings (cloid_serde).
   - Today one such null makes the bench tail's body_probe return BodyFetch::Error for the whole body (tools/bench-throughput/src/in_flight.rs:146-177). Flag on avoids that.

7. TYPES.
   - The trait at torus.rs:99 is #[rpc(server)] only, so either a Serialize-only response type or an untagged enum field works.
   - Keep RpcBlockBody's Deserialize and Vec<Value> shape for the jsonrpsee client tests (lib.rs:3665-3684).
   - Keep the camelCase field names and the #[serde(default)] attributes.

8. A/B RULES.
   - Set the flag on all 3 nodes, and at least on val2, which serves the tail.
   - Every cell must be AGREE ACCEPT with zero panic lines.
   - Report consensus timeouts and val2 rpc-worker CPU (from io-threads).
   - Run 300m as well as 10m depth 1: a faster tail changes the closed loop (300m at depth 4 gave -5.2%, n=1).
   - Run the microbench before any cells.

9. COORDINATE with item 7 step 1, which also edits torus-rpc. Rebase after it lands.

The premise holds on main a44000e0, but the headline gain does not hold for the chain.

What holds:
- get_block_body builds a serde_json::Value tree for every action.
- preserve_order really is on in the node build, so the RawValue bytes would be identical.
- The serving cost is real. On val2 the rpc-worker threads use +0.62 cores, which is 191-197 ms of CPU per body and 3.9-4.0% of fleet node CPU at 300m.

Why the claimed +3% matched/s is not a chain gain:
- At 300m the chain is exec-bound (busy 0.995-0.997, mempool about 6k, tail lag p50 1 height). The thread doing the serving is not on the critical path, so matched/s is about 0. val2's exec thread is only 0.3-0.6% slower than val0/val1, so the best case is +0.3%, below the CI.
- The 3% comes from 10m depth 1, where the bench's serial commit tail sets the pace. That is the same harness effect that tail depth 4 removes with no node code (section 70.7). The chain's 10m capacity, about 308-311k at depth 4, does not change.

What is left is unconfirmed:
- No profile of val2 exists, so the share of the serve cost that is the Value tree is not measured.
- My estimate is 47-75%, about 90-145 ms per body. That would give fleet CPU-s/1M -1.7 to -3.0%.
- It might also give back part of val2's +0.4-1.7 GB of RSS (freed memory jemalloc keeps after the serving churn). This is a new finding.

Both of these are overhead from val2 serving the bench's own commit tail. In production they matter for RPC nodes feeding the torus-explorer indexer. The rule says keep=false when the gain cannot be confirmed from data. An in-process microbench showing at least 2x would flip this to keep, as RPC serving hygiene rather than a matched/s item.

lenses.focus: The workspace has no [profile.release], and .cargo/config.toml sets only clang+mold. So the bench node (`cargo build --release -p torus-node`, tools/matched-bench/README.md:42) is built with codegen-units 16, no cross-crate LTO and the x86-64 baseline. As a result, librocksdb-sys 0.17.3 build.rs compiles RocksDB without -msse4.2/-mpclmul: software CRC32C costs ~0.57 ms CPU per 1k fills (~0.13 cores per node) under WriteToWAL in the p3cloidprof profile, and it also runs inside the ~0.6 s checkpoint batch write. Using existing profiles, estimate what lto=thin/fat, codegen-units=1, -C target-cpu=x86-64-v2/v3 and PGO (cargo-pgo trained on a 300m cell) would do for the exec thread's ~4.37 ms of wall per 1k fills and for node CPU-s/1M (23.38). Identify the hot non-generic cross-crate calls that cannot be inlined today (torus-bridge native_executor.rs into torus-core order_book/margin, the torus-state overlay, borsh, alloy) and the C/C++ dependencies that pick up target features (RocksDB, zstd, jemalloc). Design an env-only A/B (CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_* and RUSTFLAGS, no repo edit) at the 300m and 10m gate shapes, with AGREE in every cell. State arithmetic is FixedPoint (order_book.rs:9), so codegen cannot change results. Still, never use panic=abort, because exec-pool panic containment and the fail-stop hook need unwinding. Size build time and RAM (fat LTO over the revm/reth dependency tree, under the build lock shared with item 7) and portability (x86-64-v3, not native).

candidates.title: Recover EIP-712 senders with libsecp256k1, which revm already links, plus an explicit low-S check, instead of k256's recover_from_prehash
candidates.mechanism:
One function recovers every EIP-712 sender: ecrecover at crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:807-823. Its callers:
- gossip ingest: mempool lib.rs:812, recover_sender, on the torus-gossip-verify pool (torus-node main.rs:834-873);
- RPC ingress: torus-rpc torus.rs:521, validate_with_sessions, on torus-ingress-verify (torus.rs:570-584);
- exec trust-cache misses: eip712.rs:1150, recover_senders_phase1;
- the oracle-signer proof: native_executor.rs:11981.

Today ecrecover calls k256 VerifyingKey::recover_from_prehash. That runs constant-time k256 arithmetic and then fully re-verifies the recovered key (ecdsa 0.16.9 recovery.rs:312-313).

New arm, TORUS_ECRECOVER=secp256k1:
1. Keep the k256 Signature::from_slice parse and RecoveryId::from_byte(v-27). The InvalidSignature cases stay identical.
2. Reject high-S explicitly (s > (n-1)/2 gives RecoveryFailed). Today this rule is enforced only by the trailing verify (k256 0.13.4 ecdsa.rs:203, is_high).
3. Call secp256k1 0.31 RecoverableSignature::from_compact, then SECP256K1.recover_ecdsa(Message::from_digest(hash)), then keccak(serialize_uncompressed()[1..])[12..]. This is the same code as revm-precompile 32.1.0 secp256k1/bitcoin_secp256k1.rs.

libsecp256k1 recovers with a single variable-time Strauss-wNAF/GLV multiply using a precomputed G table, and has no trailing verify. It is about 5x faster than k256's recovery on the same machine.

- torus-gossip-verify: recover_from_prehash is 7,414 of 25,779 samples (28.8%); its trailing verify is 3,581 (13.9%).
- torus-ingress-verify: 3,775 of 23,827 (15.8%); trailing verify 1,799 (7.6%).
- Inside recover_from_prehash: trailing verify 48.1%, lincomb 39.2%, Scalar::invert 5.1%, decompress 3.3%, to_affine 2.9%.
- 99.7% of k256 samples sit on these two pools. The exec thread has 2 of 25,581, because exec trust-cache hits are about 100%.

**Thread cores on main code.** io-threads, hsdb-300m-r{1,2,3}-B, 9 node-cells: gossip-verify 0.94-0.97 and ingress-verify 0.76-0.84 cores per node. Recovery therefore costs 0.289x0.955 + 0.159x0.806 = 0.40 cores per node, 7.6% of node CPU.

**Recovery count (hsdb r2-B metrics).** Per node per cell: 238-239k rpc_submit_verify plus about 471.2k trust-cache misses, which equals gossip received (471,199). That is about 1,179 recoveries/s and 5.0 per 1k fills, so about 344 us of CPU per recovery under load (p4s0 gives 312 us). The 10m soak k1-b has 896k recoveries per node, 5.15 per 1k fills.

**libsecp256k1 is already in the binary.** nm of the node binary (ozarchy-p4s0-run/analyst/nm.txt) shows rustsecp256k1_v0_11_ecdsa_recover. It comes from revm 36's default 'secp256k1' feature (revm-precompile 32.1.0, which needs secp256k1 0.31.1 with recovery and global-context). The EVM ecrecover precompile already uses it.

**Speed.** Published, same machine (M2): k256 0.13.1 recover 128.5 us and verify 58.3 us; secp256k1 recover 25.6 us ([stellar/rs-soroban-env#839](https://github.com/stellar/rs-soroban-env/pull/839)). libsecp Recover is about 33 us/op in go-ethereum ([go-ethereum#31242](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/31242)) and ecdsa_recover is 33.6 us in [hive MR 689](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/hive/-/merge_requests/689); neither gives the CPU.

**History.** The s77 doc §1 (07a34c2, before hash dedup) said the verify-thread cost was Keccak, with k256 flat top symbols at about 11% of gossip-verify. Hash dedup 0ff946ea then cut gossip-verify CPU 25%.
candidates.est_gain:
**300m (exec-bound, 600 s):**
- About -0.29 to -0.33 cores per node, central about 0.31. That is 72-83% of 0.40 cores.
  - torus-gossip-verify: -0.20 to -0.23.
  - torus-ingress-verify: -0.09 to -0.11.
- Fleet: about -0.9 to -1.0 of archy's roughly 16.5 busy cores.
- CPU-s/1M: -1.24 to -1.43, which is -5.3% to -6.1% of 23.38. Computed as 5,014 recoveries per 1M fills x 248-286 us saved each.

**10m (depth 1):**
- About -0.30 to -0.40 cores per node.
- CPU-s/1M about -6% to -8.5% of 17.58.

**Other metrics:**
- matched/s, native blk/s, exec block_ms, block p99, RSS: about 0. On the bench the exec thread does no recovery, and 300m is exec-bound.
- Easing host contention might add 0 to +0.5% matched/s. That is below the ±0.85-1.3% CI, so it would not resolve.

**Overlap with other candidates:**
- bench-push-manifest-not-full-body: 0. Push copies already hit the trust cache: misses equal gossip received, and push copies go into the same channel at swarm.rs:1666.
- eip712-batch-item-keccak-x4 and ingress-market-spec-cache: additive. They remove different samples (Keccak and RocksDB) on the same threads.
- exec-carried-verified-senders and the s123 exec keys branch: 0. Exec does no recovery on the bench.
candidates.determinism:
Byte-identical by construction, then proven by tests. Both backends solve the same equation Q = r^-1(sR - zG), use the same 65-byte uncompressed encoding, and the same keccak. Edge-by-edge parity, checked against k256 0.13.4 / ecdsa 0.16.9 and libsecp256k1 in secp256k1-sys 0.11.0:
- r and s in [1, n-1]: the k256 parse stays first (InvalidSignature).
- v in {27..30}: unchanged.
- High-S: rejected explicitly with RecoveryFailed. libsecp256k1 recovery alone would accept it.
- recid 2/3: both reject exactly when r >= p-n = 0x14551231950b75fc4402da1722fc9baee. k256 rejects through a U256 overflow or through decompressing an x >= p; libsecp rejects through fe_cmp against p-n. Below that bound both use x = r+n.
- Non-residue x: both reject.
- Identity result: both reject (from_affine in k256, gej_is_infinity in libsecp).
- z: both reduce mod n.

Consensus-critical through the trust cache: senders recovered at gossip or ingress seed exec's cache (mempool lib.rs:832-834). A parity bug would therefore change exec state on that node. So parity tests gate any bench, and a mixed-fleet cell must AGREE.
candidates.flag:
TORUS_ECRECOVER:
- secp256k1: this candidate.
- k256-noverify: the sibling candidate.
- shadow: compute both, k256 is authoritative, count mismatches.
- unset, empty or anything else: today's recover_from_prehash.

Parsed once (OnceLock) by a pure parser, like TORUS_PARALLEL_VERIFY at eip712.rs:1099-1114. Node-local; a mixed fleet is safe once parity is proven.
candidates.impl_size: S. About 50-70 lines in eip712.rs (flag parser, secp arm, shadow arm). One dependency line in torus-types/Cargo.toml, using the same secp256k1 0.31 that revm-precompile builds, so no second C build. The workspace already needs cc for sha3-asm. About 250-350 lines of tests and a 40-line microbench.
candidates.test_plan:
1. **RED tests first.** Keep today's code verbatim as the reference. For each arm, compare the result variant and the address value.
   - a. 1,000 random keys x random hashes, v=27/28: Ok(signer).
   - b. Malleated twin (s' = n-s, v xor 1): Err(RecoveryFailed). This is the must-fail case; libsecp alone would return the signer.
   - c. r=1 with s=(n-1)/2: Ok. With s=(n+1)/2: Err.
   - d. r or s in {0, n, n+1, 2^256-1}: InvalidSignature.
   - e. v in {0, 1, 26, 31, 255}: InvalidSignature.
   - f. v=29/30: r=2 and r=p-n-3 give Ok. r=p-n and r=2^256-n (each hits a different k256 rejection path) give Err.
   - g. r=5 (non-residue x): Err.
   - h. Constructed identity case (R=(z/s)G, z != 0): Err.
   - i. Hash in {0, n-1, n, 2^256-1}: equal results.
   - j. Junk signature r=[31;32], s=[43;32] (mem 5c690146): the same arbitrary address.
2. **Differential fuzz.** Seeded, at least 10^7 cases in release, outside bench windows: valid signatures, twins, random bytes with v in 25..32, values biased to ±3 around 0, (n-1)/2, n, p-n and 2^256-n. Optionally a cargo-fuzz target.
3. **Batch differential.** batch_verify_native_actions_cached_with_mode on mixed batches gives an identical Vec per arm. Re-run the mempool gossip and RPC ingress tests with the flag set.
4. **Microbench on a quiet archy.** Proceed only if secp is at least 3x faster than k256 per recovery.
5. **Optional shadow soak.** 300m, 600 s, with mismatches = 0.
6. **A/B.** 300m, 600 s, ABBA, n=3 (CPU-s/1M resolved a 0.7% step at n=3), arms unset vs secp256k1, plus one mixed-fleet cell (val0 on, val1-val2 off). Every cell must be ACCEPT AGREE. Report:
   - CPU-s/1M (expect -5 to -6%);
   - io-threads cores for gossip-verify and ingress-verify (expect -0.2 and -0.1);
   - matched/s (tie);
   - timeouts, block p99, RSS (tie).
   - Then a 10m, n=2, depth-1 check of CPU-s/1M.
candidates.novelty_check:
This is not the AVOID item 'Session keys / crypto tuning for ingress' (mem aed2e235, s367, 2026-06-17):
- **Different premise.** s367 rejected crypto work for RPC ingress latency: rpc_submit_verify was about 97% queueing and core contention on an 8-core box shared with other work, and its lever was client-side session keys. This candidate targets CPU-s/1M and verify-pool cores, which are gate metrics, and needs no client change.
- **Pool did not exist then.** 68% of recovery CPU is on the dedicated gossip-verify pool, added in dd7457e5 (T2.1, 2026-07-08), after s367.
- **The baseline moved.** Hash dedup (0ff946ea, 2026-09-29: gossip-verify -25%) and asm keccak removed the per-order work that dominated in s367 and s77. k256 is now 28.8% and 15.8% of the verify threads, counting all frames below the recovery call.
- **New facts.** 48% of every recovery is a redundant re-verify, and libsecp256k1 is already linked and already used on the consensus path (the EVM precompile).

No memory, branch or commit (git log --all -S recover_ecdsa / secp256k1:: / is_high in torus-types, mempool and rpc) uses libsecp256k1 or an explicit low-S check for native actions. No collision with s123 or in-flight work: exp/s123-exec-action-keys-parallel edits eip712.rs at lines 1075-1336 and the tests, not 799-823; item 7 and Phase 5 do not touch ecrecover.
candidates.regime: Both 300m and 10m. CPU only. The saving scales with actions per second: about 1,180 recoveries/s per node at 300m and about 1,470 at 10m.
candidates.risks:
- **C library in torus-types.** This adds a C FFI dependency to a consensus crate. The same build of the library is already linked into the node and already decides EVM ecrecover results on this chain.
- **Two checks must stay.** The explicit low-S check and the k256-parse-first order must both be kept. Without the parse first, zero r or s fails with RecoveryFailed instead of InvalidSignature, which changes RPC error text. Without the low-S check, high-S twins are accepted and, through trust-cache seeding, exec state diverges on that node.
- **Version skew.** Keep secp256k1 on the same version as revm-precompile.
- **Speed on archy not measured.** The 5x figure is from an M2; x86 libsecp recovery is about 33 us in two other projects. The microbench is the gate.
- **No throughput gain.** The value is CPU-s/1M and headroom on the shared host. Whether that justifies a new dependency edge is the owner's call.

candidates.title: Pure-Rust alternative: k256 recovery without the redundant trailing verify_prehash, plus an explicit low-S check
candidates.evidence:
Same profile and thread-core basis as ecrecover-libsecp256k1-backend.
- The trailing verify is 48.1% of recover_from_prehash samples on the two verify pools (5,380 of 11,189): 48.3% on gossip-verify and 47.7% on ingress-verify. Every one of those samples is under ecdsa::hazmat::verify_prehashed.
- An independent check: on the same M2, k256 verify is 58.3 us of the 128.5 us recovery, 45% ([stellar/rs-soroban-env#839](https://github.com/stellar/rs-soroban-env/pull/839)).
- Removable: 0.481 x 0.40 cores per node = 0.19 cores per node.
- alloy-consensus 1.8.3 (crypto.rs:374-389, in the local registry) has to normalize s before calling recover_from_prehash, because the trailing verify rejects high-S. This confirms that low-S is the verify's only effective rule.
candidates.est_gain:
**300m:**
- About -0.18 to -0.21 cores per node: gossip-verify -0.13, ingress-verify -0.06.
- Fleet about -0.58 cores.
- CPU-s/1M about -0.83, i.e. -3.5% of 23.38. Computed as 5,014 recoveries per 1M fills x 0.481 x 344 us.

**10m:** about -0.20 to -0.25 cores per node; CPU-s/1M about -4% to -5% of 17.58.

**Other metrics:** matched/s, native blk/s, exec block_ms, block p99 and RSS about 0. Overlaps are the same as for the libsecp256k1 arm.

About 60% of the libsecp256k1 arm's saving, with no new dependency.
candidates.determinism:
Byte-identical: the same k256 arithmetic as today, minus a check that always passes once low-S holds.
- The accept set is unchanged: parse, recid 0-3, recid 2/3 handling (U256 overflow or x >= p), non-residue x, identity, low-S.
- The address is unchanged.
- Error variants are unchanged: InvalidSignature for parse and recid, RecoveryFailed for everything else.

It is consensus-critical through trust-cache seeding at gossip and ingress, so it carries the same proof burden: KATs, a differential test against recover_from_prehash, and a mixed-fleet cell that must AGREE.
candidates.flag: TORUS_ECRECOVER=k256-noverify, the same OnceLock flag as the libsecp256k1 arm. Unset gives today's code.
candidates.impl_size: S. About 30-40 lines in eip712.rs, no Cargo changes. It shares the test suite with the libsecp256k1 arm, about 250 lines.
candidates.test_plan:
Same suite as ecrecover-libsecp256k1-backend: the KATs a-j, a differential fuzz of at least 10^7 cases against recover_from_prehash, and the batch differential. The twin and s=(n+1)/2 cases are mandatory, because they are the only inputs where the dropped verify acted.

Add a pin test: if k256 or ecdsa is upgraded, the differential suite must re-run. The copied code tracks recovery.rs:286-310.

Microbench: expect about 45-48% less time per recovery. The A/B is a third arm of the same 300m 600 s ABBA n=3 campaign: CPU-s/1M (expect -3.5%), verify-pool cores, AGREE in every cell.
candidates.novelty_check:
Same AVOID analysis as ecrecover-libsecp256k1-backend: s367 (mem aed2e235) was about ingress latency and session keys on an 8-core box, before the gossip-verify pool existed and before hash dedup.

Nobody has measured or proposed the redundant trailing verify before. The s77 doc §1 attributed verify-thread cost to Keccak. No memory, branch or commit touches is_high or normalize_s in torus-types.

Not in-flight work. It does not collide with the s123 branches.
candidates.risks:
- **Hand-copied crypto.** The recovery code is copied from the ecdsa crate, about 25 lines, and could drift on a k256 or ecdsa upgrade; the differential test catches drift.
- **Smaller gain.** About 60% of the libsecp256k1 arm.
- **Same trust-cache coupling.** If the low-S check is omitted, high-S twins are accepted at ingest, and that node's exec diverges.
- **No throughput gain.**

result.notes:
I found two candidates, and they are alternatives, not stackable. Build both as values of one flag, TORUS_ECRECOVER, in one branch with one shared parity suite. A/B them as unset vs secp256k1 (plus k256-noverify as an optional third arm). Both cut CPU only: matched/s stays about 0, since 300m is exec-bound and the exec thread does no signature recovery on the bench.

**Overlap with other candidates:**
- bench-push-manifest-not-full-body: no ecrecover overlap. Pushed copies arrive through the same inbound channel (swarm.rs:1666-1675) and hit the trust cache (mempool lib.rs:809). Trust-cache misses (471,202) equal gossip actions received (471,199), so each foreign action is recovered exactly once per node.
- eip712-batch-item-keccak-x4 and ingress-market-spec-cache: additive. They remove different samples on the same threads (Keccak and RocksDB rather than k256).
- exec-carried-verified-senders and s123 exec-action-keys-parallel: no overlap on the bench, because exec does no recoveries there.

**Side findings, not proposed:**
- Gossipsub ed25519 signing and verification takes about 25% of tokio-rt-worker, about 0.11 cores per node (d3cba5e2: sha512 22%, curve25519 3.4%). Changing the signing or validation mode is either a network-wide change or weakens gossip-layer authentication, so it is not node-local.
- EVM sender recovery uses alloy-consensus with the k256 backend. It could move to alloy's secp256k1 backend once item 7 raises EVM traffic; today that traffic is about 0.
- Restart replay and DA-pulled bodies (exec trust-cache misses) would also get about 5x cheaper. This is qualitative only.

**Your question: where the paused branches left off.** Branch heads are checked with git log; the build and review status comes from the prior-work brief and the branches' notes files. All four are on origin and paused in archy's queue until 18c says the tests pass.
- origin/exp/s123-parallel-cancel-all-book-pass at 73c99111 (WIP): unclear. The commit message says "compile fixes in progress (not yet building or tested)". The notes file in the same commit says the previous commit d2a7562c built and passed. 18c needs to confirm which is true.
- origin/exp/s123-propose-defer-on-exec-queue at 662e5fab: code only, never compiled. Two consensus-timing review fixes are still pending.
- origin/exp/s123-exec-action-keys-parallel at 129ca92f: code only, not built.
- origin/exp/s123-defer-book-blobs-in-layer-merge at 5296115f: code only, not built.
- The other 11 refuted s123 candidates cannot be recovered here. They exist only in 18c's wf_443f7b55-fcb transcripts and /home/18c/projects/wt/exp-s123/.

**Memory:** saved the lens findings, tagged project:torus-hyperbft and lens:signature-recovery.

**Method:** read-only; no cargo, tests or benches were run. The CPU figures come from existing perf stack dumps, io-threads files and metrics on archy. The scripts are in /tmp/ecrec-lens/.

**Sources:**
- [stellar/rs-soroban-env#839](https://github.com/stellar/rs-soroban-env/pull/839): k256 vs secp256k1 recover and verify timings on an M2.
- [go-ethereum#31242](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/31242): libsecp256k1 Recover is about 33 us/op.
- [hive MR 689](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/hive/-/merge_requests/689): libsecp256k1 ecdsa_recover is 33.6 us.
- [reth secp256k1 docs](https://reth.rs/docs/reth_revm/precompile/secp256k1/index.html): states the C backend is faster than k256.

candidates.title: Lazy shard custody: build erasure shards when a peer asks for one, from the whole body already in the DA store, instead of encoding and writing all n shards for every block on hotstuff-algo
candidates.mechanism:
New node-local value TORUS_SHARD_CUSTODY=lazy. Unset or 1 keeps eager custody (today's production default); 0 keeps custody off (the bench). Under lazy, two things change.

1. custody_native_shards_core returns before doing any work at all three call sites (proposer produce_block, validator full-block path, validator compact path). That removes the RS encode, the Merkle hashing, the action re-hash, the re-serialize and the ~7.4 MB WriteBatch into cf_native_shards from the consensus thread.

2. serve_native_da_shard, on a get_shard miss, reads the raw bincode body with NativeDaStore::get_raw. These are exactly the bytes eager custody shards: same key compute_action_hash, same bincode. It encodes them under ErasureParams::for_validator_set(|SharedState.validators|), building Merkle levels once, and returns the requested index with its proof, root, k, n and body_len. If the validator set is empty it answers present=false.

The derived shard is byte-identical to an eagerly stored one for the same (body, k, n), because erasure.rs is deterministic. So mixed eager/lazy fleets interoperate. The fetcher's existing checks are unchanged: verify-then-reconstruct, one consistent (root, k, n, len) group, k distinct sources, and the body-hash backstop.

The durability contract is kept:
- The S459 whole-body mirror is untouched and stays the guarantee.
- Every node that custodies today already holds the whole body. Custody always runs right after mirror_* or a DA-store reconstruct, and nothing prunes cf_native_pending (NativeDaStore::remove has no production caller).
- So any such node can still serve any shard index. The 'k distinct sources' property custody exists for (s338 hotspot) is preserved.
- It also improves for custody=0 nodes. Today they answer present=false, so every recovery batch burns the full 25 x 20 ms = 500 ms shard pre-step (recover_bodies_via_shards) before the whole-body pull.

candidates.evidence:
**Where the work runs.** It is all synchronous on hotstuff-algo; the bench sets neither TORUS_ASYNC_VALIDATE nor any other knob that moves it.
- Leader: inside block_build_mirror (app.rs:7130-7134 -> mirror_or_drop_native -> 6648), before the attestation, the pre-proposal push and the proposal.
- Followers: inside validate_block's decode path (6825/6896), before the vote. Quorum is 3/3.
- Only with TORUS_ASYNC_VALIDATE=1 does the follower part move to the torus-async-validate worker (app.rs:5434-5466), and it still runs before the vote.
- Call count: exactly one custody call per non-empty block per node. On hsdb-300m-r2-B val1, torus_validate_block_custody_seconds_count is 1,811 = 1,208 validate + 603 produce (body_push 603), and the sum is 1.2 ms because the flag is off.

**Cost per action** (put_shards_batch, native_da.rs:275-306):
- action re-hash, bincode re-serialize, ReedSolomon::new plus encode, merkle_root;
- then for each i in 0..n, StoredShard::from_encoded_body -> EncodedBody::proof(i) -> merkle_proof -> merkle_levels(), which re-hashes ALL n leaves for every index. That is n(n+1)/k body-equivalents of keccak: 6x at n=3/k=2, 10x at n=4, 66x at n=21.
- leaf_hash copies each shard into a fresh Vec (erasure.rs:173-179). The shard bytes are cloned again and re-bincoded.
- Total at n=3: about 6.9x body bytes of keccak.

**Body size** (summary.json, hsdb-300m-r2-B):
- 300m: orders_placed_per_exec_block 93,647 / 400 = 234 places x 20,489 B (bincode, 51 B per order) plus 125 cancel-alls = about 4.8 MB per native block. 12 MB is only the byte cap; body_push_max_bytes is 7.7 MB.
- 10m (p4gate-10m-m1-b): 29,574 placed per block, about 1.52 MB.

**Keccak calibration on archy under load: about 280-330 MB/s.**
- block_build_mirror is 20.4-22.4 ms per proposal. Most of it is compute_action_hash over about 4.24 MB of canonical preimage for the same body; the rest is the clone and the MultiGet.
- exec_verify is 16.8 ms for the same 4.24 MB of verified_cache_key preimages.
- Write cost: commit_persist_write is 6.49 ms for a 4.8 MB body, about 1.35 ms per MB.

**Custody per block per node:**
- 300m: 33 MB of keccak (about 105 ms), plus RS, bincode and copies (about 10-15 ms), plus a 7.4 MB db.write (about 10 ms) = about 120-135 ms.
- 10m: about 40 ms.

**Shards written:** 31.2 KB per place action (1.52x body). That is about 7.4 MB per block = 22.8 MB/s raw per node into the consensus DB, whose whole ingest today is 24.29 MB/s (rocksdb-consensus-LOG-val1).

**Compaction analog:** cf_native_pending (same random hash keys) costs 113.3 CPU-s of compaction per 600 s for 10.0 GB raw flushed, rewriting 53.1 GB pre-compression, with flush/compaction output of 1.6 / 6.6 GB.

**Never measured on archy.**
- All 856 cells have torus_validate_block_custody_seconds_sum <= 0.5 s.
- The cf_native_shards compaction stats in the main-code LOG are 0.
- env.sh:55-56 has pinned TORUS_SHARD_CUSTODY=0 since eed446bc.

**Shards are never read in steady state.**
- native_da_shard_recovered, served and pull_requests are 0 on all nodes in the hsdb cells.
- The only production reader is swarm.rs:376.
- Neither CF is ever pruned.
candidates.est_gain:
Measured against the production default (custody on, n=3); against the bench as configured (custody=0) the gain is 0 by construction.

**300m:**
- hotstuff-algo: -120 to -135 ms per non-empty block per node (on-CPU about 187 -> 62 ms per committed block). The view's critical path loses about 250 ms (leader build plus slowest follower validate).
- CPU: -0.39 cores/node on hotstuff-algo (-7.3% CPU-s/1M), plus -0.2 to -0.35 cores/node of cf_native_shards flush and compaction (-3.5 to -6.5%). Total CPU-s/1M -10 to -14% vs custody-on.
- Device writes: about -45 to -65 MB/s per node. Custody-on adds 22.8 MB/s WAL plus flush and about 4x compaction rewrite on top of today's 84-86 MB/s.
- Storage: about -0.7 to -1.0 TB/day/node compressed, with no prune.
- Block p99: the slowest views (7.7 MB bodies, about 200 ms custody each) lose about 400 ms.

**matched/s, a model to be confirmed by the zero-code TORUS_SHARD_CUSTODY=1 pair:**
- Model: intrinsic view about 130 ms (10m view 88 ms at 1.52 MB plus about 16 ms/MB of build/validate/persist) + 2 x 125-140 ms custody = about 390-420 ms, against today's exec-paced 315 ms.
- So custody-on production should be consensus-bound at about 950-1,050 actions/s, against 1,109 today.
- Lazy restores about +5 to +20% at 300m (central about +12%).
- At 10m (+80 ms on an 88 ms view) the effect is likely larger, about +15 to +30%.
- If the baseline shows consensus still has slack, the gain is CPU and I/O only (+0-2% matched/s).

**Larger validator sets:** eager cost grows with n(n+1)/k. At n=4 it is about 1.6x, at n=21 about 10x (about 1.2 s per block). Lazy cost on the hot path is 0.

candidates.title: Keep eager shard custody but make it linear and move it off hotstuff-algo: Merkle levels once, streaming leaf hash, reuse action hashes and stored body bytes, one background custody worker
candidates.mechanism:
Alternative to lazy-shard-custody-serve-time: choose one, never stack. It is for the case where the owner wants stored shards kept, for example ahead of Phase B. New value TORUS_SHARD_CUSTODY=async.

(a) **Linear Merkle (erasure.rs).**
- encode() builds merkle_levels once and keeps them in EncodedBody. proof(i) and StoredShard::from_encoded_body slice siblings from those levels instead of calling merkle_proof, which re-hashes all n leaves per index.
- leaf_hash streams tag||index||shard into alloy_primitives::Keccak256 (the asm backend) with no Vec copy.
- The ReedSolomon instance is built once per (k, n) and reused, not once per action (erasure.rs:294).
- Shard bytes are moved into StoredShard, not cloned.
- Keccak per body drops from n(n+1)/k to n/k body-equivalents: 6x -> 1.5x at n=3.

(b) **Hashes and bytes are reused.**
- The three call sites pass hashes they already hold: the proposer's from mirror_or_drop_native, the compact path's from compact.native_action_hashes, and one computation on the full-block path.
- No action re-hash, no deep clone.

(c) **Worker.**
- A named torus-shard-custody thread, in the DaRecoveryWorker pattern (app.rs:5147ff), receives (height, hashes, params) over a bounded sync_channel via try_send. When full it drops and bumps a counter: still best-effort, never fails the vote or proposal.
- The worker reads the raw bincode bodies with NativeDaStore::get_raw_batch (exactly the bytes sharded today), encodes them, and writes one WriteBatch per block into cf_native_shards.

Rows are byte-identical to today's (legacy_put_shards_batch oracle, native_da.rs:492). The durability contract is unchanged: the whole-body mirror stays the guarantee, and custody stays additive and best-effort.

result.notes:
**Lens result.** Shard custody is the only production default here with a real cost. The answer is lazy-shard-custody-serve-time, with eager-custody-linear-merkle-offthread as a fallback. Choose one, never both.

**Measured facts.**
- **Not measured on archy.** No archy cell has ever run with custody on: all 856 cells with metrics show torus_validate_block_custody_seconds_sum <= 0.5 s, and cf_native_shards is empty in the main-code consensus-DB LOG.
- **Where custody runs.** It is synchronous on hotstuff-algo, once per non-empty block per node:
  - leader: inside block_build_mirror;
  - followers: inside validate_block, before the vote. It moves to the torus-async-validate worker only if TORUS_ASYNC_VALIDATE=1, and still runs before the vote.
- **Body size.** The task's '12 MB bodies' is the byte cap. The real mean is about 4.8 MB per native block at 300m (234 places x 20,489 B), with a 7.7 MB max; about 1.52 MB at 10m.

**Predicted result of the zero-code TORUS_SHARD_CUSTODY=1 vs 0 pair** (300m, 600 s, ABBA n=4, plus 10m):
- custody 110-140 ms per block per node at 300m (35-45 ms at 10m);
- hotstuff-algo about 0.17 -> 0.55 cores/node;
- consensus-DB ingest 24.3 -> about 47 MB/s;
- device writes +45-65 MB/s per node;
- CPU-s/1M +11-17%;
- matched/s -5 to -20% at 300m, likely worse at 10m, if 2 x custody on the critical path (about 250 ms per view at 300m, about 80 ms at 10m) makes consensus the limiter.

If the pair confirms this, the bench overstates production capacity by that margin. That is worth telling the owner even before any code. If the pair shows under 3% CPU and under 1% matched/s, drop both candidates.

**Validator count.** Today's quadratic proof makes eager custody scale as n(n+1)/k: about 1.6x at n=4 and about 10x at n=21. A larger production validator set makes custody far more expensive.

**Anti-spam A, B and D: no candidate.**
- Per action the cost is at most 2 point reads on the in-memory ReadView, 2 global-mutex operations and 1 RwLock clone:
  - A: funded.rs:124-140, called from lib.rs:1075-1093;
  - B: lib.rs:304-330, plus the charge at :1013-1015;
  - D: per RPC request, and loopback is exempt.
- That is roughly 0.01 cores/node, under 0.05% CPU-s/1M.
- The '-0.85%' from section 1 was measured with the limits OFF (env.sh). The ANTISPAM=1 cell at cap 400 (docs/plans/native-antispam-2026-10-04.md section 5, round 2) was +1.7% at n=1, 'nothing measurable'.
- Caveat for any future ANTISPAM=1 cell on today's 600 s shape: B counts each 400-order place as 400 requests against a 10k buffer + 1 per TRS traded, so it may refuse the bench's own senders. That would be a load-shape effect, not CPU.

**Other bench-vs-node differences, not pursued** (outside the lens or the reverse direction):
- TORUS_COMMIT_LAG_BACKOFF_CAP is 8 on the bench; the genesis default is 0, which turns it off. It is consensus-liveness and fleet-uniform.
- TORUS_ROCKSDB_STATS is 2 on the bench and 1 in the node, so the bench pays more, not less.

candidates.title: Move cloid upkeep off the exec thread: split the cross-market cloid index into shards by key, and run the duplicate pre-pass and the index drains per shard on the idle exec pool
candidates.mechanism:
Flag TORUS_PARALLEL_CLOID=N (unset/0/1 = today's serial code). With N>=2, CloidMarkets keeps S hash maps instead of one. The shard comes from a fixed mix of the CloidKey words (cloid low word XOR trader head word, splitmix finalizer). The cloid high word is the bench run tag, so it must not pick the shard. All methods route by shard, and snapshot() merges the shards.
(a) Duplicate pre-pass (native_executor.rs:7323-7367). It switches to the parallel path when cloid_places >= TORUS_PARALLEL_CLOID_MIN (default 2048). N exec_pool::run_jobs jobs each walk place_order_indices in flat order and take only the cloid placements whose key falls in the job's shard range. For each one the job runs CloidMarkets::live (read-only: its own shard map, then one book probe through order_id_by_cloid_key), then checks its own claimed set, sized to its share. It returns (flat index, reject message) plus the cloid_checks/cloid_books_probed counts. All placements of one key land in one job and are checked in flat order, so every verdict and message equals the serial retain. The exec thread sorts the rejects (normally zero), writes results and the DuplicateCloid metric in flat order, and runs retain only if something was rejected. The jobs mutate nothing, so if a job panics its output is dropped and the serial pre-pass runs (same outcome as today).
(b) Index drains. These are the post-match absorb loop (:7776-7781, untimed between the match and settle timers) and the stash drain over every book (:5344-5352, called at app.rs:4036 after save_books). The exec thread first moves each book's cloid log and resolved records out through a new OrderBook::take_cloid_records, which bumps log_drains exactly like drain_cloid_keys (order_book.rs:2495-2513). Then N jobs, each holding &mut to its own shard maps, apply every record of their shards in book (market) order and log order. A live record inserts (market, id). A dead record removes the entry unless it names another market: the :3332-3351 rule. When a book's log was non-empty, the job re-resolves against the read-only book, as drain_cloid_keys does. Each key's records are applied in the same relative order as the serial drain, so the index matches entry for entry. If a drain job panics, resume_unwind on the exec thread, which keeps today's failure class.

On where the paused ones left off: all four s123 branches are on c612dc7f. Main is 29 commits ahead. Among the files the branches touch, main changed only torus-consensus app.rs (+6/-4, at :1582), which does not overlap propose-defer's hunks (:806, :5750, :5971, :7577). So all four should apply onto a44000e0 without textual conflicts; I did not run a merge.
- parallel-cancel-all (73c99111): the WIP commit is rustfmt line breaks plus clippy is_multiple_of only (checked with git show). It sits on d2a7562c, which the notes report built and passed 36/36, 1784/1784 with the flag off and on, and 977/977 after the fmt changes. The subject 'not yet building or tested' looks like a stale save-point label. To resume: one build, the notes' nextest filter, then the 300m A/B. Only 18c can confirm.
- propose-defer (662e5fab), exec-action-keys (129ca92f), defer-book-blobs (5296115f): one commit each, never compiled or run (stated in their notes). Propose-defer also has the 2 open consensus-timing review fixes.

Check of the brief's split hypothesis (sections 25.2/31): refuted as the main cost at 300m.
- ModifyOrder sorts into NonGtcOrder after all cancellations (native_executor.rs:12662, sort at :12725-12744), so only CancelOrder and CancelByCloid split runs.
- Sizing from the current-main cell hsdb-300m-r2-B: 119 cancel-alls per block, 223 visits and 108 hits each, ~220 orders per level. Splitting adds no level-removal work, because choose_removal stays on per-target removal. It adds only ~300 extra group setups (~0.15-0.3 ms) and ~30-100 us of probes per by-id action.
- Probe counts imply ~75-80% of by-id actions find no order at execution.
- At 10m (deep levels, Compact) a split may cost ~0.25-0.5 ms.
- So the 2-3 ms per by-id action stays unexplained and noisy (n=1 std cells). That is why candidate 2 exists.

Conditional follow-up, not proposed: a run-preserving hoist with identical results is possible.
- Execute a CancelByCloid by S in place, without ending the run, when S has no cancel-all in the run.
- Execute a CancelOrder the same way only when the probed owner is S and neither S nor that owner has a cancel-all in the run. Otherwise the persisted CF_BLOCK_ACTION_STATUS v3 message ('belongs to X' vs 'not found') could change.
- Build it only if candidate 2 shows >= 0.3 ms per split. It edits the phase-1 loop and exec_cancel_all_run, so it waits for the s123 cancel-all branch. That branch's MIN_VISITS=64 gate already keeps small split runs serial.

Too small to propose:
- exec_cancel_order probes twice (ownership pass, then cancel pass). One pass plus get_mut on the found market would save ~15-50 us per by-id cancel.
- Modify reads price_band_bps from state once per modify.

Do not double count: the exec cleanup site (0.057, forget_cloids in phase-1 cancel-alls) moves to the pool with the s123 cancel-all branch.

Possible extension outside this lens: TraderMarkets::absorb sits in the same post-match loop. It is c0-relevant (an estimated ~22-33k sorted-Vec inserts per block at 300m) and could use the same sharded parallel drain, but its cost is unprofiled; profile it first.
