result.rationale:
I saved the round-2 summary to memory, with tags project:torus-hyperbft, machine:ozarchy, experiment-s58, type:decision and area:backend.

Decision: run round 3, and make it the last round this run allows (the design covers rounds 2-3 and stops early only on a dry round).

**Round 2 shows diminishing returns on matched/s.** 5 of the 8 checked candidates survived, but none adds resolvable matched/s at the gate shape:
- ecrecover-libsecp256k1, keccak-x4 and HW CRC32C save CPU only.
- cloid shards give exactly 0 at c0.
- view-skip-positions is RSS cleanup.
- LTO survived only as a 2-of-3 split, at about +1.4% central, which sits at the n=4 CI.
- bulk-thread-nice and lazy shard custody were refuted.

**Most of the remaining 300m exec wall already has an owner:**
- Phase 5: pass B, cache_flush, end_resident and liquidation.
- The paused s123 branches: cancel-all, the verify keys, defer-book-blobs, and the deferred ~14-15 ms sort-key keccak follow-up.
- The queued PARALLEL_ENGINE A/B: the margin-phase prepare.
- 18c's checkpoint slicing.

**Measured costs without an owner remain, so one more round is still worth it:**
- About 18-20 ms per native block of exec time that has no timer and no owner. residual_untimed is 22.6 ms, engine_untimed 12.6 ms and post_engine_tail 11.8 ms; the residual doubles from 13.6 to 26.6 ms over the cell.
- rayon idle and steal loops in the verify and exec pools. They take 20.6% of ingress-verify cycles; RPC ingress runs one install/into_par_iter per single-item submit. The total may be 0.2-0.36 cores per node.
- Full committed bodies written to the state DB's CF_BLOCK_BODIES even though the DA store already holds them. This is plausibly half of the 33.6 MB/s state WAL.
- tokio-rt-worker at 0.44 cores per node, of which only about 1/8 is attributed. The attributed part is SHA-512 from the gossipsub ed25519 envelope (Signed + Strict) plus QUIC ChaCha.
- Most of the ~100 env knobs, which have never been re-measured on current main.
- The small-action regime, which the 400-order bench never exercises.

**Expected yield:** 2-4 modest keepers, mostly CPU-s/1M and bytes written, possibly one +1-2% matched/s. Stop after round 3 unless a matched/s survivor appears.

Carried unverified into the round-3 triage: pass-a-hot-market-trader-shards, proposer-commit-on-advance-view, compact-exec-channel-handoff.

**On where the paused work left off:**
- This run re-ran the 16 cut-off and 4 unstarted round-1 verifiers from scratch; their partial work was not reused. Rounds 1 and 2 are complete and in memory (bfbd7612 and the new round-2 summary).
- For the 4 paused s123 branches, each notes file says where it stopped. Only 18c can settle whether the cancel-all branch builds, because its commit message and notes disagree. Only 18c can also name 11 of the 14 refuted s123 candidates.

lenses.title: Exec-thread time that no timer covers, after the owned items are subtracted
lenses.focus: At 300m 600 s on main code (ozarchy-hsdb-300m-r2-B val1 summary.json), 47 ms of the 312.7 ms exec block has no sub-timer: residual_untimed 22.6, engine_untimed 12.6 and post_engine_tail 11.8 ms, and the residual roughly doubles from the first to the last 60 s (13.6 to 26.6 ms) as blocks grow. Subtract the parts that already have an owner: the sort-key keccak in sort_native_actions_indexed (~14-15 ms, 18c's deferred s123 follow-up), cloid upkeep (0 at c0), the s92 telemetry loop and MatchRequest derefs (folded into r1 survivors) and the liquidation step (Phase 5). Then attribute the remaining ~18-20 ms by code region. The regions are: torus-consensus app.rs exec path 3256-3364 (overlay build), 3555-3602 (bundle seed, header put, begin_resident outside its wait), 3909-3965 and 4036-4140 (per-action nonce overlay puts, take_pending_fills, detach_resident, freeze, drop(ctx) on the exec thread, pipeline_handoff); torus-bridge native_executor.rs execute_batch 7048-7165 and the untimed spans of execute_batch_phases (7165-7259 flatten plus the ~94k-entry results init, 7605-7612, 7758-7797); and the non-liquidation tail (core-writer drain, governance, fees, epoch boundary). Map the existing exec-thread cycles:u samples (ozarchy-p4s0-run/analyst/p{1,2}-mperf-w1-exec-inline.script.gz with the a2l cache; bench-archive ozarchy-p3cloidec prof-B) onto these regions and propose off-thread drops, removed clones or allocations, or batched overlay work, each with ms per native block. Avoid the sort key, verify and trust-cache keys, cancel-all, pass B / cache_flush / end_resident (Phase 5), the match-results drop already in the pass-B scatter survivor, and the epoch barrier (r1 survivor).

lenses.title: CPU spent by idle rayon workers in the verify pools and the exec pool
lenses.focus: Cycle-weighted p4s0 profiles (d3cba5e2, 300m) put rayon idle/steal at 20.6% of torus-ingress-verify cycles (~0.16 cores per node on main, where that group uses 0.76-0.84 cores) and 3.6% of gossip-verify. About 14% of exec-pool samples fall outside match and settle-plan frames (not yet split into idle and other work), and the global pool's 32 threads exist only for the phase-1 par_recover fork-join. Together this may be 0.2-0.36 cores per node (4-7% of node CPU), the largest CPU item no candidate attacks. Examine how work reaches each pool: one rayon spawn per gossiped action (torus-node main.rs:826-875); spawn_blocking plus install/into_par_iter per RPC submit, usually on one item (torus-rpc torus.rs:566-584 and 762-794); two or more fork-joins per native block on the 32-thread exec pool (exec_pool.rs:20-60, market_workers.rs:183-222, native_executor.rs ~8698); and par_recover on the global pool (torus-types eip712.rs:1073-1300). Split idle, steal and wake cost per pool from the existing all-thread dumps (cycle-weighted via perf script -F tid,time,period, per the ecrecover check's method note) and from io-threads. Then propose right-sized pools, fewer wakeups per job, or parking (non-spinning) workers for one-job-at-a-time callers, judged on CPU-s/1M and exec runqueue wait. Avoid nice or priority changes (bulk-thread-nice refuted), CPU-set pinning (refuted), moving ingress onto the global pool (s352 regression), the exec-pool start skew (fine-grain-jobs survivor), and caps that only make sense with three nodes on one host.

lenses.title: Committed block bodies stored twice: state-DB CF_BLOCK_BODIES and the DA store
lenses.focus: dispatch_to_exec writes every committed block's full bincode body (~5 MB at 300m) to the state DB's CF_BLOCK_BODIES on the consensus thread (persist_committed_block_durably_timed, torus-consensus app.rs:1441-1497; commit_persist_write 7.7-8.4 ms per call). The same actions are already durable by hash in the DA store (cf_native_pending, in its own consensus RocksDB since a44000e0 and never pruned on main). At ~5 MB x 3.1 blocks/s that is plausibly half of the state DB's 33.6 MB/s WAL, plus the bodies CF flush and compaction (~7 + 15.5 s per node per 600 s per the r1 state-write lens), CRC and memtable work. Examine whether a compact record (header plus the action-hash list the CompactBlock already carries) with DA reconstruction can serve every CF_BLOCK_BODIES reader (boot replay_gap / load_replay_body, block sync, torus_getBlockBody, the EVM arm), and what crash ordering the two RocksDB instances would then need. Size it from ozarchy-hsdb-300m-r*-B (sampler.csv torus_rocksdb_* per DB, io-ticks write_bytes, consensus_by_node commit-persist timers, rocksdb-LOG per-CF compaction) as device bytes per fill, CPU-s/1M and consensus-thread ms. Avoid the checkpoint batch and its slicing (18c), moving the commit manifest (judged inferior in sec 74.6), and DA BlobDB and push-manifest (r1 survivors). A slower getBlockBody would also slow the 10m depth-1 bench tail; that is a harness artifact, not chain capacity.

lenses.title: Networking CPU on tokio-rt-worker: gossipsub envelope signatures, QUIC AEAD and the unattributed rest
lenses.focus: tokio-rt-worker burns ~0.44 cores per node at 300m (user 0.335 + sys 0.10 in ozarchy-hsdb-300m-r2-B io-threads), the only top-five thread group no lens has attributed. Two parts are known. First, SHA-512 from gossipsub MessageAuthenticity::Signed with ValidationMode::Strict (torus-network behaviour.rs:94 and 135): an ed25519 envelope is signed and verified on every gossip message whose payload already carries an EIP-712 or validator signature. It costs 2.36% of node cycles at 10m (ozarchy-p4soak10-run/analyst/perf/commsym-b-k1-b.txt) and ~0.5% at 300m (bench-archive ozarchy-p3cloidprof frames-self.txt). Second, QUIC ChaCha20-Poly1305 costs 0.84% / 0.56%, and AES-GCM with AES-NI may be cheaper. Attribute the remaining ~0.3 cores (per-message protobuf and bincode copies, gossipsub duplicate handling before dedup, message ids, syscalls at 23% sys) from the p4s0 all-thread dumps by tokio tid. Then propose cuts with a CPU-s/1M estimate and a safety argument: peer attribution and scoring without envelope signatures, and cipher negotiation across mixed versions. Avoid the push-manifest A/B and gossip early dedup (r1 survivor), getBlockBody JSON (r1), UDP buffer size (no gain), QUIC idle timeout (refuted), inline bodies (refuted) and shard custody (r2).

lenses.title: Census of env knobs whose defaults predate Phase 3/4 and the own-DB split
lenses.focus:
crates/ reads about 100 TORUS_* env vars, and only about 20 have been A/B'd on recent main (see the prior-work brief). Cover each remaining perf-relevant knob:
- RocksDB: TORUS_DB_WRITE_BUFFER_MB, CHURNY_CF_WRITE_BUFFER_MB, ROCKSDB_MAX_WRITE_BUFFERS, MAX_BG_JOBS, MAX_SUBCOMPACTIONS, BYTES_PER_SYNC_MIB, ROCKSDB_L0_*.
- Pipeline: ASYNC_POST_FLUSH, ASYNC_VALIDATE, DEFERRED_EXEC_READY_BYTES, EXEC_REWRITE_DURABLE_ROWS, INCREMENTAL_ORACLE, LIQ_VALUE_SUM.
- Network: GOSSIP_QUEUE_LEN, D2L_BATCH*, CONSENSUS_DIRECT_FAN, CONSENSUS_GOSSIP_MIRROR, DIRECT_PUSH_BODY_BYTES, BODY_PUSH_MAX_BYTES.
- Caps at the 400-order shape: NATIVE_TOTAL_BLOCK_CAP and NATIVE_PER_BLOCK_CAP, only with a block p99 guard; the small-action angle belongs to small-action-regime.
For each, record the default and file:line, and when and on which build it was last measured (git log -S, docs/perf, memory). Then judge whether its mechanism touches a cost that is large on main now: exec ms per fill, rocksdb:low at 5% of node CPU, both DBs' memtables in RSS after the split, or in-window state-DB waits. Output ranked zero-code A/B arms, each with an expected effect and the metric and n that would resolve it. Exclude knobs already measured, queued or owned: PARALLEL_ENGINE*, CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_MS, WAL cap, PIPELINED_WRITE, APPEND_CF_CODEC, WAL_COMPRESSION (already on the owner's re-decide list), admission, throttle and exec-queue knobs, MALLOC_CONF decay, DEFER_*_FEED, SHARD_CUSTODY, HASH_ONLY_PUSH_THRESHOLD, BOOK_ROWS, TRADE_HISTORY, CANCEL_BATCH, MATCH/SETTLE_WORKERS, and anything that reshapes the checkpoint batch (18c's slicing).

lenses.title: Small actions: what caps throughput at 1-50 orders per signed action
lenses.focus: The standard shape submits 400-order batches (run-cell.sh BATCH=400). On it, per-action fixed costs and the 400-action proposer cap never bind (NATIVE_TOTAL_BLOCK_CAP plus 64 actions per sender, torus-mempool rate_limit.rs ~56-130), and the 12 MB bytes cap and 200k orders cap are far away. At 1-50 orders per action that cap allows only 400-20,000 orders per block. Each action also pays its own fixed costs: a full ecrecover (~0.33-0.37 ms CPU; today 5 per 1k fills), EIP-712 domain and typehash work, canonical hashing at several sites, mempool, DA, nonce, replay-guard and action-status entries, and a gossip message. Oct-4 cap-20/50 cells (mem 6d0308a6, pre-Phase 3) also showed 45-60 ms of exec per small block. From code and existing cells, estimate small-action capacity on main for each binding limit: action cap, verify-pool CPU, per-block fixed exec cost and consensus cadence. Propose fixes that existing knobs can verify (BATCH; TORUS_NATIVE_TOTAL_BLOCK_CAP is proposer-local and fork-safe), or small code changes, and that do not regress the 400-order shape. Avoid inline small bodies (refuted, liveness), arrival-order selection (refuted), session-key crypto tuning (s367) and anti-spam settings (r2 lens). Do not re-propose the ecrecover and keccak-x4 survivors; cite them as dependencies.

candidates.title: Match epilogue: feed the cancel-all trader index one trader at a time, skip the triggered-stop walk when nothing triggered, and clear per-book scratch inside the match job
candidates.mechanism:
After matching, the serial epilogue loop in execute_batch_phases (native_executor.rs:7771-7796) does three kinds of unowned work.

(1) TraderMarkets::absorb (3500-3511) goes market by market. For each logged new trader it does a HashMap probe on a ~5k-trader map, a binary_search in that trader's ascending Vec<MarketId> (up to ~223 entries, about 1.8 KB), and a Vec::insert (3460-3466). About 25.5k entries are re-inserted per block, because every cancel-all take()s a trader's whole entry and the next places rebuild it. Each insert therefore touches a different cold per-trader Vec, about 110 ns each.
- Batched arm: drain each book's new_traders log into a small per-call scratch map, trader -> Vec<MarketId>. Only about 240 traders place in a block, so the map stays L1/L2 resident.
- Markets arrive in ascending order because market_results is sorted by market_id first (7771).
- After the loop, do one probe per trader, then either move the scratch Vec in (the common case: the entry is absent after a cancel-all) or do a linear sorted merge with dedupe.
- The (trader -> ascending markets) set and the entries count come out identical.

(2) The loop runs triggered.extend(r.result.triggered_stops.iter().cloned()) over every MatchResult (7787-7789). That is ~94k cold ~200-byte results per block, and on the bench shape it almost always yields nothing.
- Add a per-book triggered-stop counter (torus-core order_book.rs, bumped where a stop fires) or a MarketBatchResult field filled by the worker.
- The serial walk then runs only for markets whose count is > 0. Order stays market-id / result / trigger.

(3) Optional arm: move clear_reduce_only_positions and clear_account_margins (7781, 7786) to the end of the market's match job, after capturing charged_maker_fills for the telemetry counter. Best co-implemented with parallel-match-setup, which builds the same per-book state at the job's start.

The s92 counter loop (7790-7795) is NOT included: it is folded into sell-top-up-stitch-list part (b).

candidates.determinism:
Node-local only.

TraderMarkets is never hashed or persisted. It only selects which books a cancel-all visits; it is a superset, and an extra entry costs one probe. The batched absorb leaves the same per-trader ascending market set and the same `entries` count before any reader sees them. The readers are the next cancel-all (take/remove), the s104 size gauge at app.rs:3905, and the liquidation / single cancel paths.

The one real hazard is a dropped entry. That would leave orders on a book on one node only, which means DISAGREE, so the merge must be exact and is tested against the carried-vs-rebuilt snapshot every block.

Triggered stops:
- They reach run_triggered_stops in the same market-id / result / trigger order.
- The gate only skips the walk of markets whose trigger count is 0.
- PlaceResult.triggered_stops is read nowhere else on the batch path (only 7788).

Clears: they are book-local, batch-scoped scratch that is already cleared before settle. Moving them to the job's end is equivalent once charged_maker_fills is returned first.

With the flag off, the code path is exactly today's.

candidates.title: Write a hash-list body record (tag 0x02) to CF_BLOCK_BODIES for DA-backed commits and rebuild bodies from the DA store on read (TORUS_BODY_RECORD_COMPACT=1)
candidates.mechanism:
WHAT HAPPENS TODAY
- dispatch_to_exec calls persist_committed_block_durably_timed on the consensus thread.
- That call bincode-encodes the full committed body: about 6.1 MB for a 400-action 300m block.
- It writes the body into CF_BLOCK_BODIES in one state-DB WriteBatch, together with the header and the manifest delete.
- Every native action of a compact-datum commit is already durable in the DA store (cf_native_pending), keyed by its full-signature hash. That store is in the consensus DB since a44000e0 and is never pruned.
  - Followers rebuilt the block from the DA store.
  - The leader's S459 mirror (mirror_or_drop_native) wrote any missing bodies before proposing.

THE CHANGE (TORUS_BODY_RECORD_COMPACT=1)
- For DA-backed commits, write a tag-0x02 record instead of the full body: bincode(native_action_hashes, evm_transactions, core_writer_actions), about 11.5 KB.
- Everything else stays as today: the same batch, the same header, the same manifest delete and the same DurableRows. Exec still skips its rewrite.
- The hashes come from the pass dispatch_to_exec already runs for the mempool prune, moved ahead of the persist. No new hashing.
- The full-datum arm of on_committed_block (legacy or non-compact) keeps the 0x01 record.
- The commit-manifest put and its lifecycle are not touched.

READERS decode 0x02 with one DA MultiGet:
- load_replay_body and replay_committed: pass in the mempool's DA handle (it is in scope in try_new).
- materialize_owned, Durable arm.
- recovery_exec_source: map a 0x02 record to ExecSource::Compact, so a DA miss heals by a peer pull. Today's Durable hole has no hashes and cannot do that.
- torus_getBlockBody: use RpcState.mempool.get_native_da_batch. A miss must be a loud error, not null, or the bench tail spins.
- eth get_body: its callers read only evm_transactions, which are inline, so no DA read.

CRASH ORDERING BETWEEN THE TWO ROCKSDB INSTANCES
1. Invariant: for every hash in a 0x02 record, the DA put's WAL write has completed before the state-DB batch is issued. This holds by construction:
   - RocksDB makes a write visible to MultiGet only after its WAL write.
   - The leader mirrors before it proposes.
2. SIGKILL: both WALs are in the page cache, so nothing new is needed.
3. Power loss with TORUS_SYNC_WAL_ON_COMMIT=1: fsync the consensus WAL BEFORE the state write. Today sync_wal runs both syncs after the write. The fsync count is unchanged.
4. Power loss with sync off: neither DB is guaranteed today either. A surviving 0x02 record whose DA rows were lost heals by the ExecSource::Compact peer pull.
5. Retention: DA rows must outlive the records that point to them. Main never deletes DA rows (NativeDaStore::remove has no production caller). Any future DA GC must key off the body pruner's cutoff.

candidates.evidence:
Sources: all 9 node-cells of /home/oz/bench-results-matched/ozarchy-hsdb-300m-r{1,2,3}-B. Their crates are identical to main. Per node, per 600 s cell, unless noted.

CONSENSUS THREAD (metrics-before/after)
- torus_commit_persist_seconds totals 26.9-29.2 s per run, mean 11.75-12.76 ms per committed block.
- Load-window mean (consensus_by_node.load) is 14.1-15.0 ms per committed block.
  - body_encode: 3.20-3.41 ms mean (7.3-7.8 s per run).
  - persist_write: 6.17-6.80 ms mean (14.1-15.6 s per run).
- On r2-B val1 every persist_write is at most 64 ms and about 98% are at most 16 ms. So the cost is CPU (software CRC, memcpy, write syscalls), not queueing.
- io-threads, hotstuff-algo: 110.6-116.7 CPU-s per run (stime 7.4-10.0 s), write_bytes 9.9-10.3 GB. About 92% of those bytes are the body WAL.

BODIES COLUMN FAMILY (rocksdb-LOG EVENT_LOG parse; script /tmp/claude-1000/bodylens/cfparse.py)
- cf_block_bodies: 70 flushes per run, 9.41-9.46 GB of memtable data in. Full blocks are about 6.1 MB raw.
- 1.30-1.31 GB written to L0 SSTs (LZ4, 7.2x). Flush wall 9.4-10.0 s.
- 14 compactions turn 1.06 GB into 0.56 GB (ZSTD), costing 15.3-15.8 CPU-s.
- The whole state DB: compaction 37.6-40.6 CPU-s; flush wall 33.5-36.1 s, which matches rocksdb:high CPU of 43-46 s once the consensus DB's ~9.4 s is added.

SHARES OF WRITES
- torus_rocksdb_wal_bytes is 21.3-21.4 GB per node (35.5 MB/s). Bodies are 44% of it.
- io-ticks write_bytes is 49.9-51.0 GB per node in the bench window: 83-85 MB/s, 364-372 B per fill.
- Bodies (WAL + L0 SST + compaction output) are 11.1-11.3 GB = 81-83 B per fill = 21.9-22.6% of device writes.
- cancelled_write_bytes is 0, so WAL pages really reach the disk.

MEMORY (metrics-1hz)
- memtable_bytes{cf_block_bodies} averages 50-80 MB, which is 36-44% of the state DB's memtable bytes.

NODE CPU
- Whole-run node CPU (proc_cpu_by_node): 3,175-3,195 s on val0/val1, 3,546-3,560 s on val2, over 141.0-141.7M fills. That is the 23.38 CPU-s/1M baseline.

10m (p4tail10 r1-a1/a4: the Phase 4 node 2a245321, same body path, shared DB at the time, 303 s)
- commit_persist 17.8-20.7 s.
- Bodies 5.7-6.3 GB in, flush 5.3-6.1 s, compaction 10.0-11.7 s.
- Together about 33-38 s of 1,442-1,880 node CPU-s.
- Bench tail (tail.txt): full-body fetch p50 is about 265 ms at depth 1. The tail lags 53-67 heights, which is older than the ~4 s DA memtable turnover.

WHY THE 0x02 RECORD IS SAFE
- COMPACT_PROPOSALS is const true.
- The only pending_proposals insert is the leader's, after the S459 mirror.
- No production code path deletes cf_native_pending, and none disables the WAL.

candidates.novelty_check:
NOT NEW AS AN IDEA, BUT NEVER BUILT OR MEASURED
- s64 proposed moving the ~4 MB body-record write to the exec side: docs/perf/s64-exploration-2026-09-24.md:199.
- An s65 explorer proposed 'Make the commit manifest the durable body record': run wf_432acae7-a30, angle body-storage-format, in docs/perf/s65-explorers/killed-runs-finished.json.
- The s68 synthesis (docs/perf/s65-explorer-synthesis-2026-09-27.md:56-60) deprioritised all ~60 CPU-efficiency ideas.
- No memory, branch or commit rejects it on its merits.
- Its s65 rationale (+3-6% matched/s from consensus-thread time) was later refuted (s66-s72 consensus-thread cuts were flat; s123 consensus-reuse-action-hashes) and is NOT claimed here.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE
1. Phase 3 coalescing made bodies the biggest state-DB writer: 44% of the state WAL and 22% of node device writes. The s65 WAL split had them at about 10%.
2. Body volume is 15.5 MB/s per node, up from 5.2 MB/s (6.1 MB blocks at 3.1 blk/s).
3. a44000e0 put the DA store in its own RocksDB, so a two-WAL crash ordering is needed. It is specified above.
4. The s65 design kept the manifest row and folded the manifest put into the dispatch batch. That now overlaps section 74.6's manifest analysis. This variant writes a separate 0x02 record and leaves the manifest put and delete as they are.
5. The bench now reads bodies (IN_FLIGHT_TAIL=commit), which the s65 idea assumed it did not.
6. Per-cell LOGs now measure the background cost directly.

NOT ON THE AVOID LIST
- Not the checkpoint batch or its slicing.
- Not moving the commit manifest.
- Not DA BlobDB (r1 already dropped its cf_block_bodies arm).
- Not push-manifest.
- Not the s123 hash reuse: it adds no keccak and removes bytes.

candidates.risks:
- Retention coupling: a 0x02 record is readable only while the DA store keeps its rows.
  - Main never deletes DA rows.
  - The RH4 GC (4077726a, only on origin/perf/p3-throughput, 128-block retention) must not land unless it keys off the body pruner's cutoff.
  - Boot replay depth (checkpoint interval plus exec lag, about 110 heights) must stay inside DA retention.
- Losing or corrupting the consensus DB alone now also loses the local body log. Recovery then needs a peer pull or block sync.
- Power loss with sync off can leave a 0x02 record whose DA rows were lost. That heals by peer pull, not locally.
- With sync on, the fsync must be reordered (consensus WAL before the state write).
- Downgrade: binaries older than this change reject tag 0x02 as corrupt. The flag-off build still decodes 0x02.
- Overlap with other r1 survivors:
  - hw-CRC32C: cuts the same body-WAL CRC, so about 0.2 points of this gain shrink.
  - da-cf-blob-files: if DA values move to blob files, every 0x02 read pays a blob read plus ZSTD decompress at the tail and at boot replay. A/B the two separately.
- The bench tail at 10m depth 1 may read 0.5-2% lower matched/s (a harness artifact).
- The EVM arm (committer) still writes full records for EVM blocks. There are none on the bench; item 7 owns that path.

result.notes:
I found one candidate under this lens, and it is not a new idea. s64 and an s65 explorer proposed it; the s68 synthesis deprioritised it as a CPU-efficiency idea, and it was never built or measured. The candidate cites that history and lists what changed since. It claims no matched/s gain. Its value is CPU-s/1M (-1.4 to -1.6% at 300m, about -2% at 10m), device bytes (-22% per fill), the state-DB WAL (-44%), a small RSS cut, and archive disk growth.

All the sizing comes from the hsdb-300m-r{1,2,3}-B cells: metrics-before/after, metrics-1hz, io-ticks, io-threads, and the per-CF rocksdb-LOG parse. The parser is at /tmp/claude-1000/bodylens/cfparse.py. The 10m numbers come from the p4tail10 cells (the Phase 4 node, same body path).

Considered and dropped:
- Moving the body write off the consensus thread (s64): it moves the cost, it doesn't remove it.
- BlobDB, FIFO or universal compaction for cf_block_bodies: r1 already dropped the BlobDB arm, and FIFO deletes archive data.
- Skipping the EVM arm's body rewrite: there is no EVM traffic on the bench, and item 7 owns that path.
- DA GC after commit: it would not lower compaction within a cell, and it conflicts with the r1 BlobDB survivor.
- Any change to the manifest put: on the avoid list.

On the user's question ("do we even know where the paused ones left off?"): this lens did not study the paused branches. I checked only their git heads. All 4 origin/exp/s123-* branches sit on c612dc7f:
- parallel-cancel-all-book-pass is at 73c99111 (2 commits). The commit message says "compile fixes in progress (not yet building or tested)". The notes file in that same commit has a "Build and test results (s123 builder)" section saying d2a7562c compiled and listing follow-up fixes. The conflict is real and only 18c can settle it.
- defer-book-blobs-in-layer-merge (5296115f), exec-action-keys-parallel (129ca92f) and propose-defer-on-exec-queue (662e5fab) are one code commit each from 07:02 today. The brief describes them as never built.

Memory saved: s124 r3 bodies lens, tagged project:torus-hyperbft.

candidates.evidence:
Gaps between commits, from 'on_commit_block fired' log lines inside the bench window (my script /tmp/knobcensus/gaps.py).

10m default gate shape, tail depth 1:
- **ozarchy-p4gate-10m-m1-a** (Phase 4 node 2a245321, the newest 10m cells; no 10m cell exists on a44000e0):
  - 22-23 gaps over 1 s per node, adding up to 39-40 s of the 120 s window.
  - Of those, 9-10 last 1.15-1.35 s and 8 last 2.3-2.9 s (timeout, then doubled timeout).
  - Block p99 is 1,322-1,336 ms; headline consensus timeouts are 25 (m1-b: 24, m2-a: 20).
- **ozarchy-p4tail10-10m-r1-a1** (300 s):
  - 62-63 gaps over 1 s per node, about 102 s in total; p99 1,326-1,342 ms; 52 timeouts.
  - 0 'header re-send' lines on all three nodes.
- **Counterfactual** (replace every gap over 1.1 s with 0.3 s): p99, mean of 3 nodes, goes 1,331 -> 530 ms (gate cell) and 1,333 -> 537 ms (tail10 cell).
- **Depth 4** (p4tail10-r1-a4): only 1-8 gaps over 1 s, so little changes there.

Why these stalls are rate-limit drops (memories 8d5ce8bc, ae716181, ee2fd1ca):
- 92-100% of stalls follow at least 25 views/s.
- Honest traffic is about 2 gossip messages per author per view, against a bucket of 50.
- Timeout classes run about 1 leader to 2 no_proposal.

300m (hsdb-300m-r2-B, main code):
- Gaps over 1 s are not rate-limit driven: about 3 views/s means roughly 6 messages/s per author.
- val0's bimodal gaps (969 under 100 ms, a cluster at 0.7-1.0 s, 129 over 1 s) are the T5.2 floor, not this.
- So the 300m p99 is unaffected. Only the bench-start ramp stalls go, worth +0.1-0.25% matched/s in 600 s cells (ae716181).

Never measured: 0 of the 567 archy cells with node-env-all.txt set TORUS_HEADER_RESEND_MS.
candidates.determinism:
Node-local timing only. A leader re-sends its own header, already broadcast and byte-identical (same block hash), over the direct path.
- Receivers vote at most once (highest_view_voted).
- The equivocation check compares hashes, which are equal.
- The body fetch already running is kept.

No state, selection, ordering or validation change, so AGREE is unaffected. Mixed values across validators are safe because each leader controls only its own re-send cadence.
candidates.flag: TORUS_HEADER_RESEND_MS=250 (existing knob; unset = 3000 ms = exactly main; optional third arm =150). Passed via run-cell EXTRA_ENV.
candidates.impl_size: zero code (env only, same binary a44000e0)
candidates.novelty_check:
git log -S TORUS_HEADER_RESEND_MS finds only b4fd5b2f (2026-09-28, s75 fix D, the rejoin fix). Docs mention it only as a kill switch (docs/perf/s75-rejoin-and-pinning-2026-09-29.md:34). No archy cell has run a non-default value. It is not on the survivor, rejected, AVOID or archy-queue lists.

Prior mention: adversarial check ee2fd1ca of round-1 survivor hold-light-proposals-under-consensus-rate-limit named it as an untested zero-code probe ('recovers dropped headers but does not pace empties'). The mechanism differs from that survivor's code: this recovers drops on the unlimited path, while the survivor holds light proposals. It is the cheapest way to get the p99 gain with no build.

Risks:
- **300m re-sends:** at 300m (views about 315 ms) a 250 ms interval re-sends in roughly half of led views; 150 ms re-sends 1-2 times per led view. Each re-send means a few direct header messages per second and one QC re-check on the receiver: under 0.1% CPU, plus INFO log lines.
- **Other drops stay:** stalls not caused by header drops (dropped AdvanceView or TimeoutVote) remain.
- **Round-skip use:** followers one view behind take the round-skip path more often. It is the default-on rejoin path, but at this rate it has not been exercised under load.
- **Overlapping owner:** the symptom is the same as the round-1 survivor; coordinate.
- **Excluded alternative:** TORUS_CONSENSUS_DIRECT_FAN=1 also bypasses the limiter, but it removes the pacing: the idle chain would run at about 270 views/s and flood tiny blocks into exec and the depth-1 tail, which is the survivor's own caveat. So it is not proposed.

result.notes:
Census result: one arm. None of the assigned knobs has a credible zero-code gain on main a44000e0. Of the 567 archy cells that record their node env, none set any of them (apart from the BLOCK_CAP bundle), so none has ever been A/B'd on archy. Evidence is hsdb-300m-r2-B (sampler, RocksDB LOGs, metrics) plus the p4gate and p4tail10 10m cells.

**RocksDB knobs** (crates/torus-state/src/db.rs). All are read once at DB open and apply to both DBs since the split.
- **DB_WRITE_BUFFER_MB** (1024, :1605; 769d7b3b, 07-26, stability fix, never perf-tested): inert. State-DB memtables average 173-181 MB, p95 about 300 MB, max 528-585 MB, so the budget never binds. The consensus DB budget is a constant 256 MiB (:380) and averages about 75 MB. Combined memtable size is unchanged by the split (74.1: 245 MB in A vs 183 + 75 MB in B). The peak is the post-checkpoint flush backlog, which a lower cap cannot remove; mean RSS would fall by 50 MB at most, below the RSS noise.
- **CHURNY_CF_WRITE_BUFFER_MB** (unset = 128 MiB, :1569; 06de7326, 07-20; part of the July 18c bench env at =16 in book mode 2): inert. With Classic books and checkpoints, each 15 s checkpoint flushes about one memtable. The book CF did 27 flushes and used 1.4 CPU-s of compaction per 602 s. Any change is worth under 0.2% CPU, and a larger buffer costs RSS.
- **ROCKSDB_MAX_WRITE_BUFFERS** (4, :531) and **L0_SLOWDOWN / L0_STOP** (unset = 20/36, :801) (both 2eb62ce5, 08-19): inert. stall_micros is 0 in both DBs, L0 files peak at 4-5, and immutable memtables average 0.12 or less.
- **MAX_BG_JOBS** (4, :1541): inert. Since the split, both DBs share 3 LOW threads and 1 HIGH thread: the same rocksdb:high thread id appears in both LOGs. Compactions run about 0.27 threads on average. The wait from memtable switch to flush start is 10-102 ms at p50 and about 0.6 s at most, with no stalls.
- **MAX_SUBCOMPACTIONS** (unset, :1548) and **BYTES_PER_SYNC_MIB** (1, :1555): inert. Subcompactions only parallelize a job, and range sync covers SSTs only; section 71.4 found 0 s in balance_dirty_pages.
- **Big costs no knob can reach** (except APPEND_CF_CODEC, which is excluded), per node per 602 s:
  - DA CF compaction: 118.5 CPU-s (41 jobs, 8.31 GB in, 7.53 GB out; random keys, so full write amplification);
  - state positions compaction: 19.9 CPU-s;
  - state bodies compaction: 15.6 CPU-s;
  - state-DB flush raw: bodies 9.43 GB, positions 7.74 GB (51.9M entries), books 3.84 GB.

**Pipeline knobs** (crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs)
- **ASYNC_POST_FLUSH** (off, :817): inert. The exec body-rewrite count is 0 on main because durable rows are skipped since 1adb76eb. July's note already rated it 'NEUTRAL in vivo'.
- **ASYNC_VALIDATE** (off, :607): never run with the flag on. validate_block averages 9.3 ms, and consensus-thread cuts have been flat.
- **DEFERRED_EXEC_READY_BYTES** (64 MiB, :837): only active with nonblocking dispatch, which is excluded.
- **EXEC_REWRITE_DURABLE_ROWS** (:503), **INCREMENTAL_ORACLE** (bridge state_root.rs:51/85) and **LIQ_VALUE_SUM** (:1134): these only add work.

**Network knobs**
- **GOSSIP_QUEUE_LEN** (512; a2caa6da): inert, slow-peer events are 0.
- **D2L_*** (forward_batcher.rs:213-242): inert, 0 d2l envelopes on the bench shape. Item 7 changes EVM forwarding.
- **CONSENSUS_DIRECT_FAN / GOSSIP_MIRROR** (config.rs:110-132): never A/B'd. Not proposed, because it removes the limiter's pacing (see the candidate's risks).
- **DIRECT_PUSH_BODY_BYTES** (8 MB floor, caps.rs:109): lowering it equals the round-1 survivor's manifest arm and touches the excluded HASH_ONLY knob.
- **BODY_PUSH_MAX_BYTES** (0, hard cap 64 KiB, implementation.rs:3605-3673): in July it gave +7% at idle and was neutral under saturation. At 300m vote_delay is about 8 ms at p50 and about 0.1 s at p99, hidden behind exec back-pressure.

**Caps** (torus-mempool rate_limit.rs)
- **NATIVE_PER_BLOCK_CAP** (64, :58): inert against MAX_IN_FLIGHT 4.
- **NATIVE_TOTAL_BLOCK_CAP** (400, :105) binds in 96% of 300m blocks. About 11-14% of exec time does not scale with actions (save_books 21.5 ms with all 300 books dirty, checkpoint settle 8.6, upkeep 1.1, replay guard 3.2). So +20% cap gives about +1.5-2% matched/s but about +15-20% p99, and pushes bodies over the 8 MB push floor. -20% cap costs about 2.5-4% matched/s for -15-20% p99. Neither passes the p99 guard.

**Other knobs checked**
- **VERIFIED_SENDER_CACHE_CAP**: evictions equal inserts minus 64,000 exactly, and exec hit rate is about 100%.
- **PARALLEL_VERIFY=1**: under 0.1 ms; already the zero-code first step of survivor exec-carried-verified-senders.
- **COMMIT_LAG_BACKOFF_CAP**: fleet-uniform, so not node-local.
- **CHECKPOINT_MAX_BYTES**: reshapes the checkpoint batch, so excluded.

**Paused work** (the user's question): where each paused item stopped is recorded in the prior-work brief (s123 branches 73c99111 / 662e5fab / 129ca92f / 5296115f, and archy's paused queue). This arm needs no build and can run on archy while those wait for 18c.

Memories saved: the census note and the arm note (tags s124-round3, env-knobs).

candidates.title: Order-charged proposer budget for small place actions: a block of 1-50-order places holds about as many orders as a 400-order block, while the 400-order shape's selection stays byte-identical
candidates.mechanism:
Today SelectionWalk charges every action one of 400 slots: full() is selected.len() >= limit and take_cancels compares counts. At 1-50 orders per action a block therefore carries only 400-20,000 orders, while the 12 MB bytes cap and the 200k orders cap sit idle. New proposer-local flag TORUS_NATIVE_MIN_ACTION_ORDERS=c (unset = off, 1..=400, arms 50 and 100). With it on:
- A PlaceOrder or PlaceOrderBatch costs min(400, max(c, n_orders)) units.
- Every other action (cancels, oracle, modify) costs 400 units.
- The budget is action_cap x 400 units. paced_selection_caps tiers scale it as they scale action_cap today.
- full() and offer() test units. A budget miss is Skipped, so a smaller action can still fill the tail. Bytes and orders stops stay deterministic-prefix Stops.
- The cancel share stays in count terms (ceil(limit x 25%)), unchanged.
- For small places, the per-sender cap and the trust-cache default (64 x max actions per block x 5/2) scale by 400/c, so exec does not lose its recover skip.
At the 400-order shape every action costs exactly 400 units, so the selection is identical to flag-off. A small-action block holds up to 400 x 400/c actions: c=100 gives 1,600 (up to 160k orders at b=100, ~16k at b=10), c=50 gives 3,200. Bigger blocks amortize the per-view and per-block fixed costs instead of adding views. Views are capped by the gossip limiter, and the hold-light survivor would pin them at 20/s.

candidates.evidence:
**Action cap x cadence ceiling.** At b<=50 the only selection limit that binds is the 400-action count. The bytes and orders caps stay below 10% (376*b orders and ~100 KB-1 MB per block).
- Light-block cadence on current-main-like cells: idle_blk_s 18.0-21.5 (hsdb-300m-r1..r3-B) and 16.2-18.8 (p4gate/p4tail10 10m).
- The cause is the consensus gossip limiter: swarm.rs:1494 and config.rs:280, 50 msg/s per author at ~2 msgs per view, so ~25 views/s, then 1.2 s stalls (mem 8d5ce8bc, ae716181).
- When not limited, blocks with 1-50 400-order actions commit at p50 9.5-10 ms intervals (val1 logs, p4gate-10m-m1-a and p4tail10-r1-a1). The p4tail10 a1 cell had 80 stalls over 1 s.
- Oct-4 main-cap20 (cancel-only blocks): 21.9 blk/s, 51 timeouts.
- Ceiling: ~6.4-8.8k actions/s. At b=1 that is ~5-7k matched/s; at b=10, 60-83k orders/s (~47-64k matched/s at matched/placed 0.77-0.79).

**Verify CPU (next limit).** hsdb-r2-B io-threads at ~1,110 actions/s per node: gossip-verify 0.94-0.97 cores, ingress-verify 0.76-0.84 cores, tokio 0.44, rpc 0.17.
- That is about 1.3 ms per gossip-verified and 2.2 ms per ingress-verified 400-order action. Item hashing is ~1 us/order and ecrecover ~0.34 ms.
- A small action costs about 1.5 ms of fleet CPU (3 recovers ~1.0 ms + ~0.4 ms per-action overhead + bench signing).
- On 16C/32T that gives a ~11-13k actions/s ceiling, about 30-50% above the cap ceiling.

**Per-block fixed exec cost.**
- 10m: regression intercept 5.7-6.4 ms per native block (blocks with <=200 actions, val1 logs). Oracle-only blocks take 1.8-2.1 ms (torus_exec_oracle_only_block_seconds); the liquidation step takes 1.8-2.9 ms. Not binding.
- 300m: 25-45 ms per block regardless of size:
  - liquidation step 8.1-8.6 ms (120 s cells) and 11.3-12.7 ms (600 s cells), scanning 1,470-1,620 traders every block (LIQ_SCAN_PER_BLOCK 2,048);
  - Classic save_books 9.5-21.5 ms (native_executor.rs:6259 borsh-encodes the whole book of every dirty market; 376*b orders over 300 markets dirty nearly all books);
  - checkpoint settle wait 3.7-8.7 ms.
- So at 300m: b=10 runs ~47-67 ms per block (exec co-binds with the cadence at 15-21 blk/s); b=50 runs ~85-125 ms (8-12 blk/s), ~165-240k orders/s against 295k placed/s at b=400.

**Correction.** In mem 6d0308a6 the 45.7 and 60.7 ms 'per small block' are 1/blk_s, the block interval. Exec chain was 3.75 ms (cap20, cancel-only) and 39.5 ms (cap50). Those cells ran BATCH=400.
candidates.est_gain:
Small-action shapes only; the 400-order shape is unchanged by construction. matched/s is capped by verify CPU after the lift:
- 10m, b=1-10: +25-50%.
- 300m, b=10: +40-60%. Exec-amortized blocks reach 110-140k orders/s before CPU binds.
- 300m, b=50: +25-35% at c=100 (80k-order blocks at about today's ~300 ms block time).
- 10m, b=50: about 0-10% (cap, CPU and exec co-bind near the 400-order shape).
- Once the libsecp256k1 ecrecover survivor lands (fleet cost ~0.7 ms per action, ~25k actions/s ceiling), b<=10 could reach about 2.5-3x.
Other metrics: native blk/s falls (bigger blocks); exec block_ms per block rises; CPU-s/1M falls a few % at 300m small (per-block fixed costs amortized); 10m light-block 1.2 s limiter stalls should drop because views are no longer sub-40 ms.
candidates.determinism:
Proposer-local selection policy only, the same doctrine as TORUS_NATIVE_TOTAL_BLOCK_CAP (rate_limit.rs:97-99).
- validate_block, check_proposal_data and the exec entry check only datum structure, hash, parent link and header native_action_count == body length. Nothing rejects on action, order or byte totals.
- Execution is deterministic for any committed body, so mixed flag values across validators cannot fork.
- Flag-off: unit cost 1 and budget = limit reproduce today's count test exactly.
- Flag-on at BATCH=400: every action costs 400 units, so the selection is identical.
candidates.flag: TORUS_NATIVE_MIN_ACTION_ORDERS=c (unset/0 = off; 1..=400; arms c=50 and c=100). Zero-code precursor: BLOCK_CAP=N bundle (TORUS_NATIVE_TOTAL_BLOCK_CAP plus companion caps and trust-cache size).

candidates.test_plan:
**Step 0, zero code, before any build.** run-cell.sh at 10m and 300m, 120 s, standard shape (OPEN_ORDER_BUDGET=900, MAX_IN_FLIGHT=4, IN_FLIGHT_TAIL=commit, RETRY_BUSY=1, SUBMIT=1).

- Order: n=2 smoke per pair, then ABBA n=4 on pairs that move.

result.notes:
**Your question: where the paused ones left off** (git, read-only)

All four s123 branches are based on c612dc7f. Each is 1-2 commits ahead of main and 29 commits behind main a44000e0, and none has been rebased.
- **origin/exp/s123-parallel-cancel-all-book-pass @ 73c99111** (WIP on top of d2a7562c). The commit message says "compile fixes in progress (not yet building or tested)", saved when the build lock went to item 7. Resume steps it gives: build, run the notes' tests, run the flag-off suites, then replace the WIP commit. Its own notes file says something different:
  - d2a7562c built cleanly;
  - 36/36 targeted tests passed, plus a mutation check;
  - 1784/1784 rdeps passed with the flag off and on;
  - 977/977 torus-bridge passed after the clippy and rustfmt touch-ups.

  So we know where it stopped, but not whether the WIP state builds. 18c must confirm.
- **origin/exp/s123-propose-defer-on-exec-queue @ 662e5fab**: code only, never compiled. Two consensus-timing review fixes are still pending.
- **origin/exp/s123-exec-action-keys-parallel @ 129ca92f**: code only, not built.
- **origin/exp/s123-defer-book-blobs-in-layer-merge @ 5296115f**: code only, not built.

Where the 18c side stopped beyond this is only in 18c's workflow files, which are not on archy.

**Small-action capacity on main** (archy, 3 validators; b = orders per action)

| Limit | 10m | 300m |
|---|---|---|
| (1) Action cap x light-block cadence | 400 actions x 16-22 blk/s = 6.4-8.8k actions/s. Binds first at b<=10. | Same ceiling |
| (2) Verify CPU | ~1.5 ms fleet CPU per small action, about 85% of it the 3 ecrecovers: ~11-13k actions/s | Same |
| (3) Per-block fixed exec | ~6 ms: never binds at b<=10, co-binds at b=50 | 25-45 ms: makes b>=10 exec-bound at ~15-21 blk/s, and b=50 reaches ~165-240k orders/s vs 295k at b=400 |
| (4) Consensus cadence | The gossip limiter, not per-view work. Light views take ~10 ms when not limited. | Same |

Bench caps do not bind at small b: the per-sender limit of 64 (MAX_IN_FLIGHT=4), the 25% cancel share (cancels are ~5% at b<=50), the 12 MB bytes cap and the 200k orders cap.

**Dependencies to cite**
- libsecp256k1 ecrecover survivor: the dominant per-action CPU.
- keccak-x4: item hashing is ~1 us per order per node, which matters at b>=20.
- hold-light-proposals: it pins cadence at 20 views/s or less, which makes bigger blocks the only lever left for small actions.
- ingress-market-spec-cache and push-manifest: smaller per-action items.
- exec-carried-verified-senders: the per-action exec verify.
- parallel-classic-book-save, s123 defer-book-blobs, Phase 5 step 3 and the liquidation scan: the 300m small-block fixed cost. Small blocks raise their weight by 3-8x.

**Small-action ideas I checked and dropped as too small**
- Per-call EIP-712 domain separator (eip712.rs:213-224 runs 4 short keccaks, ~1.5-2 us against a ~340 us recover).
- Single-action RPC verify inline, skipping the rayon install hop at torus.rs:776 (~1-2% CPU).
- Batching gossip-ingest spawns (main.rs:870, ~1% fleet CPU).
- Replay-guard nonce multi_get (~1-2 us per action).
- Switching book mode (not node-local, and already on the AVOID list).
- Per-sender pool cap (that belongs to the anti-spam lens).
- The direct fan: kept only as a test arm, since it belongs to the cadence survivor.

**Correction on a memory**: the "45-60 ms of exec per small block" from the Oct-4 cells (mem 6d0308a6) were block intervals, not exec time.

Scripts are in /tmp/smallact (execwall.py, cadence.py). Memory saved under project:torus-hyperbft, s124-round3.

candidates.title: Send native-action pre-spread batches over the existing authenticated /torus/direct 0xFD fan (zstd per peer, no relays) instead of signed, raw gossipsub
candidates.mechanism:
Today each node flushes admitted actions every 50 ms, or at 128 KB or 1,024 actions, and gossipsub-publishes the batch raw on /torus/native-actions/1.0. The cost of that path:
- **Signing.** MessageAuthenticity::Signed makes the swarm task SHA-512 the whole batch twice for the ed25519 envelope (Behaviour::publish -> build_raw_message).
- **Verifying.** ValidationMode::Strict makes every receiver's connection task clone, re-encode and SHA-512 every received copy in GossipsubCodec::decode. This happens before the duplicate cache.
- **Relays.** All validators are gossipsub explicit peers, and explicit peers are kept out of the mesh. IDONTWANT goes only to mesh peers, so every receiver relays each batch to the other validators. Each batch arrives about 1.55 times.
- **Bytes.** Everything crosses QUIC uncompressed, encrypted with ChaCha20-Poly1305. The zstd gossip topic was removed in s364 because gossipsub cannot negotiate compression per peer.

With TORUS_NATIVE_PRESPREAD_DIRECT=1:
- publish_native_batch builds `0xFD || u64-LE count || concat(per-action bytes)`. The per-action bytes are already `bincode::serialize(&(sender, action))` (bincode 1.3.3, fixint), so this is a valid `bincode(Vec<(Address, SignedNativeAction)>)`, i.e. exactly the pre-proposal and B1 envelope format.
- It sends that envelope to every connected mapped peer through `direct.send_request`. This reuses fan_native_push's target resolution but uses a dedicated PushScheduler instance. It does not use pending_native_pushes, the dial nudge, recent_native_bundles re-push retention, or the info log.
- /torus/direct/2.0 is negotiated per peer and zstd-compressed at level 3, with a bomb-guarded decompress. Old peers fall back to raw /1.0.
- The QUIC/TLS connection authenticates the sender, and verify_sender_key checks it against the peer map.
- Receivers need no change: on main the 0xFD branch already feeds the same native_action_inbound channel, hence the same add_native_action_from_gossip verify, trust-cache and pool path, as gossip.
- Consensus and tx topics keep Signed/Strict gossipsub unchanged.
- What disappears for native batches: envelope sign and verify, relay copies, gossipsub protobuf, message-id and mcache work, and about 90% of the QUIC bytes.

candidates.title: Prefer TLS_AES_128_GCM for libp2p QUIC (libp2p-tls hardcodes ChaCha20-Poly1305 first)
candidates.mechanism:
libp2p-tls 0.6.2 builds both client and server rustls configs with CIPHERSUITES = [CHACHA20_POLY1305, AES_256_GCM, AES_128_GCM]. rustls servers follow the client's order by default. So every QUIC connection uses ChaCha20-Poly1305, plus scalar ChaCha20 header protection (ChaCha20_ctr32_nohw per packet).

The 5950X has aes, vaes, vpclmulqdq and avx2, and ring 0.17.14 has the VAES/VPCLMULQDQ AVX2 AES-GCM path, which is about 2.5-3x cheaper per byte. AES header protection is a single AES block.

With TORUS_QUIC_AES_FIRST=1, a [patch.crates-io] copy of libp2p-tls 0.6.2 (about 10 changed lines) reorders the client list to [AES_128_GCM, AES_256_GCM, CHACHA20]. The server keeps honouring client order, so peers without AES hardware are never forced onto AES.
candidates.evidence:
- **300m (p4s0 W1 val1, 13,936 tokio samples):**
  - AEAD seal/open plus header protection: 1,398 user samples = 0.037 cores per node at hsdb scale (8.5% of tokio).
  - ChaCha20_ctr32_nohw header protection alone: about 0.005 cores.
  - The p3cloidprof frames-self file puts ChaCha at about 0.56% of node CPU.
- **10m (p4soak10 commsym-b-k1-b):** chacha20_poly1305 seal 0.44% + open 0.40% of node cycles.
- **CPU:** /proc/cpuinfo on archy lists aes, pclmulqdq, vaes, vpclmulqdq and avx2.
candidates.est_gain:
- Without the first candidate: about -0.026 cores per node (about 60% of bulk AEAD plus most of header protection). CPU-s/1M about -0.4% to -0.6% at 300m and about -0.6% at 10m. matched/s 0.
- After the first candidate cuts QUIC bytes about 90%: about -0.05%.
- This is at or below the CPU-s/1M resolution for n=4 600 s cells.
candidates.determinism: No state impact. Only the per-connection AEAD changes. Payloads are byte-identical after decryption. With the flag off, the cipher list and rustls config are identical to today's.
candidates.impl_size: About 10 lines in a vendored libp2p-tls 0.6.2 via [patch.crates-io]. The cost is maintaining a vendored dependency.
candidates.test_plan:
**Unit tests:**
- Client config suite order with the flag on and off.
- QUIC handshakes for flag-on->off, off->on, on->on and off->off all succeed.
- A flag-on dialer negotiates AES_128_GCM (check rustls negotiated_cipher_suite in the vendored config path or with a debug log).
- A soak crossing at least 2^23 packets on one connection survives quinn's key updates.

**Bench:**
- Fold it into a CPU-only A/B: 300m, 600 s, ABBA n=4.
- Check that the perf symbols move from chacha20_poly1305_* to aes_gcm_*_vaes_avx2.
- Run it only if the first candidate is rejected.
candidates.novelty_check:
- Not in any AVOID or prior-round item. QUIC idle timeout and UDP buffers were different knobs.
- The brief named this lens. No memory or document records a cipher change.
- **Mixed versions are safe.** TLS 1.3 always picks a suite both sides offer, and all three remain offered by both sides:
  - connections dialed by a flag-on node get AES-128-GCM;
  - flag-off pairs keep ChaCha20;
  - QUIC Initial packets are AES-128-GCM regardless (RFC 9001 sec. 5.2).
- **Security.** AES-128-GCM is TLS 1.3's mandatory suite. ring's AES-NI/VAES code is constant-time. quinn rekeys automatically before the AES-GCM confidentiality limit (2^23 packets per key: about every 9 minutes per connection at today's about 15k packets/s, or rarely after the first candidate).
candidates.regime: 300m and 10m (CPU only; negligible if the first candidate lands)
candidates.risks:
- The gain is small and largely superseded by the first candidate.
- It requires vendoring libp2p-tls.
- Forcing AES on the server side would slow peers without AES hardware, so keep the change client-side only.
- Benefit is unresolvable at n=4 unless combined with other CPU arms.

candidates.title: Run gossip-verify jobs and single-item RPC ingress verifies on a parking executor instead of rayon, removing rayon's yield-and-steal idle loop
candidates.mechanism:
How rayon-core 1.13.0 idles: a worker that runs out of work does 33 rounds before it parks on a futex. Each round tries to steal from every other worker's deque, checks the injector and calls sched_yield. In addition, every idle worker that finds a job wakes up to 2 more sleepers (counters.rs:151-170). Those then spin the same 33 rounds and park.

How work reaches the two verify pools:
- **Gossip pool:** one rayon spawn per action, about 1,550 per second per node (gossip plus pre-proposal pushes).
- **Ingress pool:** one spawn_blocking plus install of a 1-item par_iter per RPC submit, about 390 per second per node.
So both pools pay a full wake, spin and park cycle almost per job: 0.85 parks per submit and about 0.3 per gossip job.

The change sits behind a node-local flag. The two rayon pools are replaced by a minimal parking executor (about 50 lines, in torus-types so both torus-node and torus-rpc can use it):
- Same thread count (available_parallelism / 2 = 16) and the same thread names.
- One FIFO Mutex<VecDeque<Job>>, which keeps rayon's injector order.
- Idle workers are kept on a LIFO stack and parked with std::thread::park. The dispatcher unparks the most recently idled worker, and only when one is idle. Hot threads are reused, as with rayon's lowest-index wake.
- No stealing, no yield loop, no cascade wakes.

Gossip arm:
- main.rs:870 `gossip_verify_pool.spawn(job)` becomes `parking.spawn(job)`.
- The in-flight counter and the 1024-job inline fallback stay as they are.
- A panicking job aborts the process, matching rayon's behaviour with no panic handler (registry.rs:375-384).

Ingress arm:
- When to_verify.len() == 1 (the bench shape), verify_one_action_with runs as a parking-pool job and the handler awaits a tokio oneshot. Today it runs spawn_blocking plus install.
- This also removes the blocking-pool handoff and the LockLatch wait and wake.
- Panics are caught and returned as the same internal error.
- Multi-item batches (up to SUBMIT_BATCH_MAX 100) keep the rayon install, so they still split across threads.
- The single-action JSON endpoint (torus.rs:1598-1605) already verifies without rayon.

candidates.regime: Both 300m and 10m. CPU-only (CPU-s/1M); no throughput effect expected in the exec-bound (300m, 10m depth 4) or tail-paced (10m depth 1) regimes.
candidates.risks:
1. The gain is small, at the edge of n=4 resolution. The io-threads per-group check is the primary readout.
2. The gossip pool is on the DA body-availability path (mem 24b6e781). Push bursts must still fan out to all 16 workers promptly; this needs the DA guards above.
3. Without a spin, workers park even across 10-80 us gaps, so there may be more park/unpark pairs. That cost is already in the estimate's residual.
4. Panic semantics must match: abort for gossip, error for ingress. Lost wakeups must be prevented: check the queue and push onto the idle stack under one mutex, and rely on park/unpark tokens.
5. rpc_submit_verify_cpu_seconds changes meaning on the flag-on path. Compare rpc_submit_verify_seconds instead.
6. The bench-push-manifest-not-full-body survivor removes the push bursts. The gossip arm's saving could move by about ±30%.
7. Item 7 step 1 (unpushed on 18c) edits nearby code in torus-node main.rs and torus-rpc, so expect trivial merge conflicts.
8. Moving the ingress verify onto tokio blocking threads instead (rotating through about 70 threads) would cool the jemalloc tcaches and eat part of the gain. That is why a 16-thread LIFO pool is proposed rather than inline spawn_blocking.

result.notes:
PREMISE CORRECTION (most important finding)
The lens overstated the idle cost about 2-3x, and two of its numbers are artifacts:
- **"Rayon idle 20.6% of ingress-verify cycles" (mem 4864a390):** this is the remainder bucket after keccak 31.3%, validate_known_markets 28.4% and recovery 17.6%. It holds parse_bytes hex 6.0%, decode 6.3%, verify_one_action_with self 2.7% and ReadView/oracle/alloc. The true idle-loop share is 0.93-1.25% of user cycles.
- **"14% of exec-pool samples outside match/settle-plan":** this is sample-count weighting. Idle samples carry about 1/20 of the mean period. Cycle-weighted: match 60.7%, pass A 38.2%, idle 1.0%, other 0.06%.
- **Whole rayon idle cost, including kernel yield and futex time:** about 0.1-0.12 cores per node (about 2% of node CPU), not 0.2-0.36:
  - ingress about 0.022-0.029;
  - gossip about 0.032-0.041;
  - exec pool about 0.025;
  - global pool 0.0235 (0.035 at 10m).

POOLS NOT PROPOSED
- **Exec pool:** run_jobs is the function the fine-grain-jobs survivor rewrites. Revisit after it lands; the same parking pool could back run_jobs.
- **Global pool:** already covered by exec-carried-verified-senders. New measurement for that survivor: the exec thread waits on the no-op phase-1 par_recover fork-join for 2.45 ms per native block (mean; p50 0.81, p90 7.4; p4j3 perf-sched val1). Its own zero-code first step, TORUS_PARALLEL_VERIFY=1, would bank this. Caveat: Serial mode recovers trust-cache misses serially (about 0.35 ms each), which slows catch-up.
- **Exec-thread off-CPU per block (p4j3):** match scope 19.6 ms, pass A scope 12.0 ms, checkpoint settle 9.8 ms, preemption about 7 ms. Of the 131 preemptions/s, 58% are reschedule IPIs and 25% timer ticks; 49% have no val1 successor within 20 us.

SIDE FINDINGS (not my lens)
- **Mempool write lock:** gossip threads block on it 1,485 times/s (mean 1.66 ms, about 2.5 threads blocked on average).
- **RocksDB LRU-shard mutex:** ingress threads block on it 1,460 times/s inside validate_known_markets. The ingress-market-spec-cache survivor removes those reads.
- **rayon wake-mutex stalls:** rpc-workers block on them 303 times/s at about 0.76 ms each. This adds submit latency.

Scripts and outputs are in /tmp/rayon-idle-lens/ (split2.py, ingress_parts.py, pooljobs.py, iothreads.py, swcount2.py, preempt.py, execwait.py). Two memories were saved (tags lens:rayon-idle, s124-round3, project:torus-hyperbft).

result.summary:
KEEP, minor. I could not refute this on determinism or safety. All three arms stay node-local and serial on the exec thread, or local to one book inside its own match job. The cancel-all index (TraderMarkets) is never serialized or hashed. Its only readers are take()/remove() in cancel_orders_and_stops (native_executor.rs:10863-10869, used by the single cancel-all and by liquidation_step.rs:477), exec_cancel_all_run (10964-10974) and the size gauge (app.rs:3905). So if the batched absorb leaves the exact same per-trader ascending set and `entries` count, a flag-on node, a flag-off node and a mixed fleet all reach identical state.

The one real hazard is the one the candidate names: a missing (trader, market) pair. cancel_orders_and_stops(Some(m)) skips the book outright when remove() returns false, so orders stay behind on that node and the result is DISAGREE. Extra pairs are harmless (one probe, only a telemetry counter changes).

Arm 2 is exact if the gate is derived from the worker's own results. The only producer of triggered stops is OrderBook::trigger_stops (order_book.rs:3310), and the only reader on the batch path is native_executor.rs:7788. Arm 3 is equivalent: nothing reads reduce_only_positions or account_margins between the end of the job and 7781/7786.

Panics: exec-thread panics are fail-stop (app.rs:4623 plus the node hook's exit 70; the only recovering catch, catch_recoverable, wraps settle pass A at 8651). Drained-but-not-yet-merged scratch therefore cannot carry into later execution.

Gain (outside this lens): arm 2 is probably overstated. Most of the triggered walk's cost is the first touch of about 94k MatchResults of about 240 B each. The s92 loop (metrics are always on) walks the same results right afterwards, so gating the walk mostly moves that cost into the s92 loop.

Side answer to the user's question about where the paused branches left off: 73c99111 differs from d2a7562c only by rustfmt reflow and two is_multiple_of clippy edits. The notes in that commit report those edits tested (977/977 torus-bridge with the flag off). So the commit message's "not yet building or tested" looks stale, but the branch still needs one rebuild and test run before an A/B.

- Arm 1 (batched absorb): -2.4 to -2.7 ms, plausible and not contested. The cold per-trader binary_search and insert go away, and nothing later picks up that cost.

- Arm 3 (clears in the job): -0.4 to -0.5 ms, plausible. The large-table frees move to the workers.

That is roughly block_ms -1.0 to -1.15%, so matched/s about +0.9 to +1.1% (central +1.0%) at about 0.3% per ms. This is below the n=4 CI of +-1.3%, so judge it on engine_untimed_ms and engine ms per 1k fills. 10m is about +0.1 to +0.3%, since its share came mostly from arm 2.
result.constraints:
1. Arm 1 must be exact.
- Each trader's resulting Vec must equal what the sequential absorb produces: strictly ascending, no duplicates.
- Book logs repeat traders: push_trader_order pushes on an empty entry, and every stored stop, restore_stop_row and borsh-loaded stop pushes again (order_book.rs:1606, 3416-3421, 3466, 4692). So dedupe when pushing (skip if last()==market).
- Build each Vec in the order of the market_results sort at 7771, or sort+dedup if the drain point ever moves. debug_assert ascending.
- `entries` += exactly the number of new pairs. Never insert an empty Vec.
- In the common case (entry absent) move the Vec in. If the entry exists, do a sorted merge with dedupe.

2. Drain every book's log with drain_new_traders(), whether the index is Some or None. With None, drop the log as absorb does today (3507-3509). This keeps debug_assert_index_fed (5378) and the s120 log_mark semantics. Never read the log by reference and clear it some other way.

3. Merge immediately after the loop, unconditionally, before settle, return_matched_book, run_triggered_stops and any return. Put no `?` or early return between the drain and the merge. The scratch must be empty on entry (debug_assert) and fully drained on exit, so nothing carries across calls (about 2 execute_batch_phases calls per block). Use its HashMap iteration order only for inserting into the map.

4. Arm 2: compute the gate in match_market (market_workers.rs:336-384), after the request loop, as any(!r.result.triggered_stops.is_empty()), and return it in MarketBatchResult. Do not use a torus-core counter.
- If a book counter is used anyway: bump it in trigger_stops() (3310, also reached through check_stops 2309); reset it at the start of each batch job; keep it out of the custom Borsh serialize (4577); initialise it in new() and deserialize_reader (4623); never let matching, saving or hashing read it.
- The walk must keep market-id, then result, then trigger order. An undercount means stops are never placed, which is DISAGREE.

5. Arm 3: clear inside match_market after the request loop and resolve_cloid_log. Return charged_maker_fills in MarketBatchResult for the 9.11 counter. Pass the toggle as a parameter or ctx value, not an env read in the worker, so the test callers of match_parallel and match_parallel_capped keep today's behaviour. The worker-panic path (run_contained, then the fatal at 7733-7755) stays unchanged.

6. Flag: read it once (OnceLock), plus a ctx field or Force toggle like execute_batch_cancel_mode so tests do not race on the env var. Unset or 0 must run today's code literally. A mixed-flag fleet is safe only because of constraint 1.

7. Tests: run a flag on/off differential with exact equality of trader_index() snapshots and cancel_index_size() after every block. The existing assert_index_covers_books (cancel_batch_exec_tests.rs:721) checks only the superset. Cover:
- the targeted cancel-all Some(m) path (the DISAGREE path);
- stops: stored, restored, and triggered cascades in the first and last market;
- cloids, modifies and liquidation cancels;
- the None index (first block after a load, and non-resident mode);
- a multi-call block shape.
Also run the RED planted-bug check (drop one merge, expect failure) and rdeps(torus-bridge) with the flag both ways.

8. Coordination:
- The paused cancel-all branch 73c99111 has an identical epilogue and reads the index the same way, so it is a rebase only.
- Phase 5 step 3 merges worker dirty sets in this loop.
- sell-top-up-stitch-list part (b) owns the s92 loop.
- parallel-match-setup and the pool-granularity sibling edit match_market (arm 3).

The s92 loop (7790-7795, always on with metrics), the Auto settle total_fills walk (7806-7810) and the pass-A weights walk (8631-8637) all walk the same MatchResults on the exec thread, so gating the triggered walk mostly moves its first-touch cache traffic into the s92 loop. result.summary:
The premise holds on main a44000e0, but the gain does not. The post-match epilogue (native_executor.rs:7771-7796) runs on the exec thread between the match timer and the settle timer, so it falls in engine_untimed, and it is the same code as the profiled build (d3cba5e2 7356-7381). Recounting the d3 W1 profile reproduces the candidate's sample counts: absorb 183/194, triggered walk 58/77, clears 36/24.

Two parts of the estimate are wrong:
1. Scale factor. The candidate scaled by 1.46 using 64.2k placed per block, which is the whole-cell average. The profile window W1 was 191 native blocks at 71.5k / 70.9k placed per block (prof-metrics-w1 deltas). The correct factors are x1.55 for the absorb, which scales with index churn (17.85k to 27.7k visits per block), and x1.31 for the per-result and per-book sites. Measured engine_untimed goes from 9.9 ms (W1) to 12.56 ms (main), x1.27, so the "12.3 vs 12.6" identity check is partly an artifact of the wrong factor.
2. Arm 2 mostly moves the cost rather than removing it. The disassembly shows the triggered walk's cost is a cache-miss stall on each 240-byte MatchResult (offset +0x90), plus one out-of-line spec_extend call per result. record_margin_cuts, in the s92 loop that runs right after on the same market, reads +0x80 and +0xb0, which are the same cache lines, and then does a lock add. Gating the walk therefore shifts the stall into that loop, unless it happens to hide under the existing is_buy miss.

Corrected saving is about 2.9 ms per native block with flag=2 and about 3.3 ms with flag=3, against the claimed 4.0. That is about +0.9-1.05% matched/s at 300m, about +0.2% at 10m, and CPU-s/1M about -0.2%. It is below the n=4 CI and fails the project's 0.4%/ms and 2%-of-exec-wall stop rules. There is no measurable p99 or RSS effect.
result.corrected_gain:
300m, 600 s cells (block_ms 312.7, exec busy 0.997, so the exec thread is the bottleneck):

Arm 1, batched absorb:
- Base cost on main: about 2.6-3.1 ms per native block. W1 measured 108-114 ns per cancel-all visit; main has 27.7k visits per native block (54.5M / 1,967).
- The batched version keeps the log drain, address hashing, small-map probes, Vec growth and about 240 final probes or merges, about 0.35-0.8 ms in all.
- Net saving: -1.8 to -2.75 ms (central -2.35). The candidate claimed -2.4 to -2.7.

Arm 2, triggered-walk gate:
- The call overhead goes away: 18-30 W1 samples, about 0.25-0.4 ms at main.
- The load stall (40-47 W1 samples, about 0.55-0.65 ms at main) moves into record_margin_cuts, which reads the same lines, unless the OoO core hides it under the is_buy miss.
- Net saving: -0.25 to -1.0 ms (central -0.6). The candidate claimed -0.9 to -1.2.

Arm 3, clears moved into the match job: -0.33 to -0.5 ms, scaled x1.31 instead of x1.46.

Totals:
- flag=2: -2.3 to -3.6 ms (central about -2.9), so matched/s +0.7 to +1.15% (central +0.93%).
- flag=3: central about -3.3 ms, so about +1.05%.
- The engine_untimed readout should drop by about -2.3 to -3.6 ms. The candidate predicted -3.5 to -4.4.
- 300m 120 s gate shape: about -2.0 to -2.8 ms of about 218 ms, so about +1.0%.
- 10m: about -0.3 to -0.9 ms of about 249 ms, so +0.1 to +0.35% (claimed +0.4%).
- CPU-s/1M: about -0.2%, exec thread only (arm 3 moves work rather than removing it). Not resolvable; the smallest step resolved so far is 0.7% at n=3.
- Block p99 and RSS: about 0.

Every figure is below the n=4 paired CI of +-1.3% and about the size of the n=3 600 s CI (+-0.85%).

KEEP, severity minor. This is not a redo. Nothing on the fatal list covers it: no s123 experiment, no refuted s123 candidate, no measured no-gain item, not the queued TORUS_PARALLEL_ENGINE A/B, and no in-flight work (checkpoint slicing, item 7, Phase 5). The closest prior is a sibling in this same workflow. The round-1 novelty check ee2fd1ca, on the kept candidate hold-light-proposals-under-consensus-rate-limit, already named TORUS_HEADER_RESEND_MS at about 100-150 ms as an untested zero-code probe. So this candidate is really the zero-code arm of that experiment, and it should run as arm B of the same campaign.

I confirmed the mechanism in code and in logs (details in "verified"):
- The re-send is armed when the header is broadcast. It fires only while the leader is still in its own view.
- The algorithm loop wakes when a re-send is due.
- The direct path has no rate limiter. The dual-path dedup is inactive with the direct fan off, and headers are exempt from it.
- On the receiver, a repeated header keeps the running body fetch, votes at most once, and costs one non-sync write.
- In 10m depth-1 logs the stalls are dropped headers. The leader built a block and neither follower validated anything for 0.9 s. With the 3,000 ms default the re-send never fires.

The gain is latency only, and only on the 10m depth-1 loopback shape: block p99 drops from about 1.33 s to about 0.5 s and the timeouts mostly go away. matched/s is about 0, and 300m is unaffected.

Feasibility: zero code. It is an existing node-local env knob with existing unit tests, and run-cell's EXTRA_ENV export reaches the nodes. Because no code changes, it has no file conflicts with sibling experiments. It does conflict as a measurement: do not run it in the same cells as hold-light-proposals or the other consensus-timing arms.

result.summary:
KEEP, severity minor. Under the determinism and safety lens the candidate holds. A tag-0x02 record is a node-local storage format. It is never hashed or gossiped, and resolving it gives back byte-identical actions: every DA writer recomputes compute_action_hash from the struct it stores, and that hash commits to the canonical bytes, the nonce and the full signature.

Crash safety against SIGKILL holds by construction on main. The DB options set no disable_wal and no manual_wal_flush, so any DA row a MultiGet can see is already in the WAL in the page cache. All three commit arms that would write 0x02 build their bodies from DA reads, or from a mirror that fails closed. Nothing on main deletes DA rows. Consensus timing gets slightly better, not worse.

Errors in the candidate's own safety argument (none is fatal):
- (a) 'The only pending_proposals insert is the leader's' is false. Followers insert in finish_validate (app.rs:6993-6997). The conclusion still holds, because the follower decode path is DA-backed too.
- (b) Downgrade is understated. An older binary does not just reject 0x02 as corrupt: boot replay parks an unhealable missing=0 Durable hole, the node fail-stops after the 5-minute budget, and RPC errors on those heights for good.
- (c) Sync-off power loss is a new dependency. Today the state DB alone can replay (applied, committed]. With 0x02, both WALs must survive. The existing two-DB HotStuff-state weakness already outweighs this.
- (d) The RH4 commit 4077726a adds DA GC and also TORUS_DA_DISABLE_WAL. The WAL bypass would break the SIGKILL invariant. That commit sits on 4 unmerged July branches.
- (e) The existing downgrade knob TORUS_BODY_RECORD_LEGACY_JSON must override the new flag.

The implementation must meet the constraints listed below.
result.corrected_gain:
I did not re-measure (not this lens). The safety constraints cost about nothing:
- An optional exact presence check (pinned MultiGet of about 400 keys, mostly memtable hits) costs under about 1 ms per commit on hotstuff-algo.
- With sync on, moving the consensus-WAL fsync ahead of the state write is free: still 2 fsyncs per commit.

The gain stays CPU and I/O only:
- 300m: CPU-s/1M about -1.2 to -1.6%, device writes about -20%, matched/s 0 (exec-bound).
- 10m: CPU-s/1M about -1.8 to -2%. At tail depth 1, val2's DA reads may cost the harness 0.5-2%.

Two small offsets that do not show on the bench:
- Boot replay still rewrites a full 0x01 record for every replayed height (DurableRows::default, app.rs:2212-2218 then 4369-4412).
- Heights with EVM txs get a full 0x01 rewrite at exec (commit_block_metadata, app.rs:3192). This matters once item 7 brings EVM traffic.
result.constraints:
1. WHEN TO WRITE 0x02. Write it only if all of these hold, else write 0x01:
   - A DA store is wired (mempool is Some).
   - The source is DA-backed: the compact arm, or the cached arm. The cached arm covers both the leader insert (app.rs:7206) and the follower finish_validate insert (app.rs:6996, async-validate verdict path included). A source recovered from a 0x02 record also qualifies.
   - TORUS_BODY_RECORD_LEGACY_JSON is unset (block_body.rs:46-74). That knob exists for downgrades and must win.
   - No DA write anywhere bypasses the WAL. If a TORUS_DA_DISABLE_WAL-style knob ever lands, refuse the flag or force 0x01.
   - Recommended defense in depth: run NativeDaStore::missing(hashes) right before building the batch. It is an exact pinned MultiGet, never key_may_exist or bloom. Any absent row means write 0x01.
2. WHICH HASHES. The record's hashes must be compute_action_hash of the executed actions in block order, or the committed datum's list (cached_matches_compact, app.rs:1293-1308, proves them equal). Never use peer-supplied or otherwise precomputed hashes. Every DA writer must keep keying rows by compute_action_hash of the stored struct (native_da.rs:74-123). This rule now also protects boot replay and RPC history.
3. STRICT DECODE.
   - decode_body_record without a resolver must return Err on 0x02. It must never return a body with empty or short native_actions: replay_gap would execute that as a short block and silently diverge.
   - Resolution is all-or-nothing. Check that the resolved count equals header.native_action_count.
   - A DA miss or an undecodable row makes load_replay_body return None, which parks a Hole. recovery_exec_source (app.rs:1683-1697) must map the 0x02 record plus the header from CF_BLOCK_HEADERS to ExecSource::Compact, so the heal pull gets the real hashes.
   - The EVM-only decode is a separate function, called only from eth.rs.
   - No unwrap or expect on DA results.
   - Optionally re-hash resolved actions on boot replay (boot only).
4. FLAG OFF. The 0x01 bytes must be identical to main. Keep the mempool-prune hash pass after the persist when the flag is off. The 0x02 decode branch must be reachable only through records a flag-on run wrote.
5. FSYNC ORDER AND POWER LOSS.
   - With TORUS_SYNC_WAL_ON_COMMIT=1: fsync the consensus WAL (StateDb wal_peer) BEFORE the state batch, and the state WAL after. Add a test on the order and the count.
   - With sync off (the default): document that local replay of (applied, committed] now needs both WALs. Recommend sync on for production validators that use the flag.
6. RETENTION. DA rows must outlive every 0x02 record.
   - Pruning is opt-in (main.rs:366-381), so by default bodies and therefore DA are kept forever.
   - Any DA GC must key off the body pruner's cutoff and the boot replay window.
   - RH4 4077726a (128-block GC plus WAL bypass) must not merge as-is. It is on origin/perf/p3-throughput, perf/ab-differ-theirs, feat/precompile-0800-topn-gas and perf/deep-book-storage.
7. RPC.
   - torus_getBlockBody resolves through a read-only DA batch (NativeDaStore::get_batch). Do not use Mempool::get_native_da_batch: it calls flush_da_mirrors, a DB write, from RPC threads.
   - Consider fill_cache=false, so val2's tail reads do not evict consensus-DB blocks.
   - A DA miss is an RPC error. The JSON must be byte-identical to the 0x01 reply.
8. DOWNGRADE. Document a procedure: flag off, then run until no 0x02 record is left in (applied, committed]. Or ship an offline rehydrate tool (0x02 to 0x01 via DA). Otherwise an older binary fail-stops at boot and errors on those heights forever.
9. SNAPSHOTS. create_snapshot checkpoints the state DB only (snapshot.rs:78-106), and restore replaces the whole data_dir. A future snapshot fix must carry the DA rows or rehydrate 0x02 heights.
10. TESTS TO ADD to the candidate's plan:
   - Follower cached arm and async-validate verdict both write 0x02.
   - LEGACY_JSON overrides the flag.
   - No mempool means 0x01.
   - Strict-decode and short-body rejection.
   - Sync-on fsync order.
   - A replay window mixing 0x01, 0x02 and empty blocks gives the same state digest as a flag-off run.
   - The SIGKILL cell passes AGREE and reports restart time (boot replay now does about 44k random DA reads).
11. A/B this separately from hw-CRC32C, da-cf-blob-files and checkpoint slicing. If item 7 adds a field to TorusBlockBody or CompactBlock, the 0x02 layout must add it too (pin it with a destructuring test).

result.summary:
KEEP, severity minor. My lens (novelty and feasibility) does not refute it. No rejected, measured no-gain or in-flight item covers it, and no code or branch has ever built it. It is not novel, though. The s65 explorer (docs/perf/s65-explorers/killed-runs-finished.json, [12].output.ideas[0]) already proposed moving the native pre-spread onto the /torus/direct fan. The s65 synthesis set it aside as a CPU-only item and it was never run.

I checked the mechanism in the code and it holds:
- Receivers already send 0xFD batches into native_action_inbound, the same path as gossip.
- The proposed envelope decodes byte-for-byte as the existing 0xFD format.
- Gossipsub (Signed + Strict) checks the signature on every received copy before it drops duplicates.
- Validators are explicit peers, so every batch is relayed again.

It can be built as a default-off, sender-side env flag in swarm.rs and config.rs, about 200-300 lines with tests. One design fix is needed. /torus/direct is limited to 100 open requests per connection (sending and receiving combined), and consensus votes use the same protocol. When the limit is hit, incoming requests are dropped with only a log line. So the pre-spread needs a per-peer in-flight cap.

The gain is CPU only: about -3% CPU-s/1M, with matched/s about 0.

On the paused queue: item 7 step 1, which the s123 builds were paused for, is now merged on origin/main (853fed28). origin/main is now f9ec4b2d, 17 commits past the local a44000e0.
result.corrected_gain:

Expected result:
- **300m:** CPU-s/1M about -2.5% to -4%, central about -3% (about 23.4 to 22.7). If only the envelope sign/verify and the encryption bytes go away, the floor is about -1.5%.
- **10m:** similar.
- **matched/s:** about 0 (0 to +0.3%) at both market counts. 300m is exec-bound and 10m at tail depth 1 is paced by the bench.
- **Unchanged:** native blk/s, exec block_ms and RSS.

I trimmed the candidate's figure slightly for two reasons:
- The 12.1x zstd ratio was measured on whole-block pushes of about 5 MB. Pre-spread batches are about 128 KB (about 10 actions) and will compress somewhat less.
- Each batch becomes its own request: a new QUIC stream, a protocol negotiation, a response, and a zstd context. That adds about 80 requests/s per node in each direction.
