picks.title: Encode Classic book blobs as per-book exec-pool jobs into presized buffers; keep the puts serial in market order
picks.spec:
Verified on a44000e0. Classic is the book mode on bench and testnet (TORUS_BOOK_ROWS empty). save_order_books (crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6206, called on the exec thread from app.rs:3982) forces the per-market loop for non-level modes (:6244-6251, last_save_workers = 1). Its Classic arm (:6252-6279) runs, serially per dirty book: borsh::to_vec(&*book) (1 KiB initial buffer, doubling), put_cf_raw_owned, then discard_row_ops / discard_level_ops.

save_books cost:
- 300m 600 s: 20.7-21.7 ms of a ~313 ms block; 23-26 ms late in the cell at 604-719k resting orders.
- 300m 120 s: 10-11.7 ms.
- 10m depth 4: 30-36 ms.
It is all on-CPU: 5.3-5.5% of exec samples (serialize ~60%, realloc ~22%, journal discard ~16%). The exec pool is idle at this point: run_jobs is called only by match (market_workers.rs:183) and pass A (:8698).

Change (Classic mode only, flag on only):
1. Module-level items right after `fn parse_save_books_min_ops` (:2691-2696), before `#[cfg(test)] mod save_books_workers_toggle_tests` (:2698):
   - a parser for TORUS_PARALLEL_BOOK_SAVE (on only for trimmed 1);
   - `const CLASSIC_PARALLEL_SAVE_MIN_ORDERS: usize = 16_384` (total resting orders over the dirty books);
   - a thread_local pin `Cell<Option<(bool, usize)>>` with `#[doc(hidden)] pub fn with_parallel_book_save<R>(on: bool, min_orders: usize, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R`;
   - `fn parallel_book_save() -> Option<usize>`: Some(min) when on; reads the pin, else a OnceLock over the env, logged once.
   Do not reuse TORUS_SAVE_BOOKS_WORKERS / parse_save_books_workers: unset, they default to host parallelism.
2. save_order_books: add a middle arm to `let dirty = if self.book_mode.is_level_authority() {...} else {...}` (:6244-6251): `else if matches!(self.book_mode, BookMode::Classic) && <gate> { written += self.save_classic_parallel(); Vec::new() }`.
   - Gate: parallel_book_save() is Some(min), at least 2 dirty books are present in order_books, and the sum of book.order_count() over them is >= min.
   - Otherwise today's path runs. The counter and book-mode-marker writes after the loop run unchanged on both paths.
3. New `fn save_classic_parallel(&mut self) -> usize`, placed right after save_order_books (closing brace :6359), before the mode-2 doc (:6361):
   a. Gather `Vec<(MarketId, &mut OrderBook)>` in one `self.order_books.iter_mut()` pass filtered by `self.dirty_books`, sorted by market id (as drain_level_books :6427-6434). Markets missing from order_books are skipped, as today.
   b. On the exec thread, compute a capacity hint per book: `128 + 97 * order_count() + 145 * pending_stop_count()`, saturating, capped at 256 MiB. Use it only for Vec::with_capacity. Bench orders are 97 B and a cloid order is 113 B, so a buffer grows at most once. Allocating here keeps blob RSS in the exec thread's jemalloc arena.
   c. One job per book, heaviest order_count first: `move || { let mut buf = buf; let r = borsh::BorshSerialize::serialize(&*book, &mut buf).map(|()| buf); book.discard_row_ops(); book.discard_level_ops(); r }`.
      - Run them with crate::exec_pool::run_jobs: per-book jobs plus rayon stealing; no thread::scope and no static N chunks.
      - Bytes equal borsh::to_vec, which is with_capacity plus the same serialize call.
   d. Back on the exec thread, in ascending market id:
      - Ok(Ok(data)): put_cf_raw_owned(CF_NATIVE_ORDER_BOOKS, &market_id.to_be_bytes(), data) and written += 1. A put error calls latch_save_fault with today's text 'book save: order book put (market X): e'.
      - Ok(Err(e)): today's 'failed to serialize order book' tracing::error!, and skip (no latch, as today).
      - Err(panic): latch_save_fault(&mut self.fatal_error, 'book save: encode job panicked (market X)') and no put. Never a silent skip.
   e. Set self.last_save_workers to the number of jobs (>= 2), so the torus_exec_save_books_workers gauge shows engagement. Optional, flag-on path only: record the encode wall time in save_split.drain_ns and the put loop in save_split.write_ns.
4. No changes to torus-core, OrderRows, modes 2-3, save_order_books_deferred, exec_pool.rs or market_workers.rs. No journal-skip sub-flag.
picks.tests_first:
1. Inline unit tests next to the flag items:
   - the parse table;
   - the gate: with one dirty book, or a total below min, the serial path runs and last_save_workers == 1.
2. New tests/parallel_book_save_tests.rs: a run_universe-style driver for Classic mode, adapted from tests/save_books_parallel_tests.rs :227 to BookMode::Classic with resident books.
   - Input: random places, cancels, cancel-alls, fills, stop-limits and modifies across >= 6 markets, then a reload.
   - Run it plain and inside with_parallel_book_save(true, 0, ..).
   - These must be equal between the two runs: per-block written counts; every CF_NATIVE_ORDER_BOOKS row (each blob == borsh::to_vec(book)); the next-order-id and mode-marker rows; the full CF dump or running hash; empty journals after save.
   - Mutation check: putting in descending order, or skipping a book on Err, must fail the test.
3. Fault paths, via an in-crate cfg(test) planted-panic market id or an injectable encoder:
   - a panicking encode job latches fatal_error with 'encode job panicked' and writes no blob for that market;
   - an injected put fault latches the same first fault as the serial path.
4. Env reruns:
   - `TORUS_PARALLEL_BOOK_SAVE=1 cargo nextest run -p torus-bridge -E 'binary(order_book_persist_tests) or binary(r02_load_save_tests) or binary(perf_equivalence_golden) or binary(save_split_attribution_tests)'`;
   - torus-consensus reference_paths_match_production_classic_reload and _resident (app.rs:26402, :26407);
   - then rdeps(torus-bridge) with the flag set and unset.
   The default min (16,384) may keep small fixtures on the serial path, so the pinned differential test in item 2 is what proves the parallel path.
picks.expected_gain:
Assumes a 2.5-3.5x speedup, bounded by memory bandwidth.

save_books per native block:
- 300m 600 s: 21.7 to about 6-9 ms (late in the cell, 23-26 to about 7-10 ms).
- 300m 120 s: 10.5 to about 3-6 ms.

matched/s:
- 120 s gate: +1 to +2.5% (central about +1.5%).
- 600 s: +1.5 to +3.5% (central about +2.5%).
- 10m: about 0 at depth 1; +3 to +6% at depth 4.

Other metrics: native blk/s +3-5%; CPU-s/1M neutral to -0.3%; RSS within +-0.1-0.3 GB.
picks.constraints:
- Microbench gate first: proceed only at <= 40% of serial for the 300-book shape.
- New flag. With the flag unset, never touch exec_pool::pool().
- Only the Classic arm changes.
- Jobs are pure: no self.state, metrics, commit_tx or logging inside them.
- Fork-join only. Never overlap with the next block's engine, because the books are live.
- Puts stay serial and ascending, with today's latch, log and skip behavior.
- A job panic must fail-stop through latch_save_fault; it must never become a skip.
- The capacity hint only feeds with_capacity: checked or saturating math, no assert.
- Keep the per-book encode a small free fn, so Phase 5's freeze can reuse it.
- Watch engine ms per 1k fills during save bursts (the 3 nodes share DRAM bandwidth) and RSS.
picks.conflicts:
- No other pick touches save_order_books or this anchor.
- Phase 5 step 3 (planned by 18c) moves Classic serialization to freeze but still encodes whole blobs there. Keep the encode helper reusable, and tell 18c that the Phase 5 cost table already counts save_books as removable, so the same time would be claimed twice.
- s123 defer-book-blobs (checkpoint_layer.rs) complements this pick.
- s123 cancel-all edits other hunks of native_executor.rs.
picks.bench_measure:
Run after the microbench gate passes.

Cells:

- 300m 120 s, ABBA n=4.

- block_ms with fills per block, and the share of blocks at the 400 cap

- CPU-s/1M (ANCOVA)

picks.microbench:
Gate before any cell: a new #[ignore] test, tests/classic_book_save_ubench.rs, built like tests/l3_savebooks_ubench.rs but with NativeExecContext::new_with_mode(.., BookMode::Classic, Some(holder)).

Setup:
- Fill 300 books with about 2.3k resting orders each, and separately 10 books with about 64k each.
- Use non-crossing GTC limits from many traders, added via insert_order_book or execute_batch.
- Mark all books dirty (ctx.dirty_books is pub).

Measure: time save_order_books() serial vs with_parallel_book_save(true, 0, ..), median of 20 saves.

Run it once on an idle archy and once next to a running 3-node cell, because DRAM bandwidth is shared.

Continue only if the parallel 300-book save takes at most 40% of the serial time.

knob_arms.name: wal-compression-post-phase3
knob_arms.env: TORUS_ROCKSDB_WAL_COMPRESSION=zstd (EXTRA_ENV on all 3 validators; the state DB and the consensus DB both open with DbTuning::from_env, db.rs:650 and :683)
knob_arms.rationale:
Owner decision s109 (mem bdf5b1cd): WAL compression stays off during Phase 3 and is re-decided after Phase 3 by a tw vs tw+d A/B. Phase 3 and the own-DB split are both merged now, and nobody has run that A/B.

Earlier result: in acc3, before Phase 3, the zstd arm gave +1.7% matched/s, +2.4% CPU and -83% bytes vs tw.

Expected now:
- Per node the WAL carries ~35 MB/s (state DB) plus ~26 MB/s (consensus DB), so device writes should drop sharply.
- CPU-s/1M likely +1 to +3%.

Risks:
- The ~200 MB checkpoint batch is compressed by the flush worker inside the state-DB write group, which may lengthen the in-window stall.
- commit_persist (a 6 MB body on hotstuff-algo) also pays the zstd cost.

Bench: 300m 600 s ABBA n=3-4.
- Report CPU-s/1M, device MB/s (io-ticks), checkpoint DB write and flush seconds, in-window and out-of-window block p99, commit_persist_write, matched/s, AGREE.
- Add one SIGKILL restart cell to exercise WAL replay.
- Run it separately from the push-threshold arm, since both cut consensus-DB WAL bytes.

knob_arms.name: push-threshold-production-default
knob_arms.env: TORUS_HASH_ONLY_PUSH_THRESHOLD=524288 (= the compiled HASH_ONLY_PUSH_THRESHOLD, 512*1024; devnet/wsl/env.sh:45 pins 8000000; set on all 3 validators via EXTRA_ENV)
knob_arms.rationale:
With the full-body push enabled, followers ingest every action twice, once from pre-spread gossip and once from the push. That is ~470k duplicates per node per 600 s, each paying the DA re-mirror, the key keccak and the pool write lock.

Expected:
- CPU-s/1M -3.8 to -4.9%.
- Device writes -12 to -15 MB/s per node.
- matched/s about +0.2%, i.e. a tie.

Owner call: this moves the bench baseline onto the production dissemination path. Do not flip env.sh while archy's paused queue is still pending.

Guards: AGREE, dissemination_clean, DA pull and MissingData counts, 'pre-warm pull of MISSING' lines, view_vote_delay, timeouts, gossip dropped_full = 0.

Cells: 300m 600 s ABBA n=3-4, plus one 10m pair.

knob_arms.name: header-resend-250ms
knob_arms.rationale:
Why the default does nothing: it is 3000 ms, which never fires before the 1.2 s view timeout. The 10m cells contain 0 'header re-send' lines.

Why 250 ms helps: the re-send uses /torus/direct, which skips the 50 msg/s per-author gossip limiter (swarm.rs:1494). That limiter drops leader headers during fast, light views.

Expected at 10m depth 1:
- log-based block p99 ~1.33 s down to ~0.55-0.8 s
- timeouts from ~20-25 to ~0-3 per 120 s cell
- matched/s ~0, possibly about -1% because the depth-1 tail sees more empty heights

300m is expected unchanged.

Cells: the 10m gate shape at 120 s, ABBA n=4, plus a 300m 600 s guard pair.

Report: re-send line count, view-timeout classes, round-skip and 'body validation failed' counts, AGREE.

This is latency-only and must run before any hold-light-proposals code. Coordinate with Tier 5 and item 7.

knob_arms.name: rocksdb-hw-crc32c-build
knob_arms.env: Build only: add CXXFLAGS_x86_64_unknown_linux_gnu='-msse4.2 -mpclmul' to the hsdb build.sh env. Leave RUSTFLAGS and CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG as they are. Use a separate CARGO_TARGET_DIR and pin EXPECT_NODE_MD5.
knob_arms.rationale:
Every RocksDB LOG on main reports 'Fast CRC32 supported: Not supported on x86', so every WAL byte is checksummed in software.

Expected:
- checkpoint DB write 0.60 s -> ~0.40-0.45 s
- commit_persist_write ~8 ms -> ~4 ms
- CPU-s/1M -0.8 to -1.0%
- matched/s ~0 to +0.5%

Output is byte-identical, since the CRC values are the same.

Before running cells, check that `nm` shows crc32c_3way and that both DB LOGs report 'Supported on x86'.

This changes the baseline for every later A/B, so both arms of any code A/B must use the same CXXFLAGS.

Before adopting it as the baseline, run one SIGKILL restart and reopen the DB with the other build.

knob_arms.name: parallel-verify-serial-probe
knob_arms.rationale:
At 300m, exec trust-cache hits are ~100%, so phase 1 of batch_verify does no crypto. It still forks and joins on the global rayon pool every block, and Serial mode removes that.

Expected:
- exec_verify 16.8 ms -> ~14.5-15.5 ms per native block
- matched/s +0.3 to +0.8%, below the CI

Why run it: it is a zero-code probe that measures the fork-join part of the exec-carried-verified-senders vs s123 exec-action-keys decision. Add it as a cheap third arm in any 300m campaign and report exec_verify_seconds per native block and end_resident_wait.

With the flag off the list is None, and TopUpCand::record (:793-813) does nothing, without even looking up basis. The stitch_outcome change (:8341-8372) keeps the same entry/push and only adds an Option return value. The only extra hot-path work is one flag read per execute_batch call (:7613), a per-order Option return and a no-op call, plus one log line per process.

2. Flag set: deterministic and identical to the scan (:10044-10102).
- place_order_indices is strictly ascending: it is pushed in order at :7368-7419 and Vec::retain keeps order. Both stitch loops (:7619, :7645) walk it, so the list comes out in flat order.
- k is the Vec length before the push, and pushes only append, so k stays valid.
- Nothing touches market_batches between the stitch and :7692 (only fold_out unpacking and bal_cache.merge_disjoint, :7676-7677). basis is immutable (:7535). So c.reserved equals p.margin_reserved and c.res_qty equals the scan's res_qty.
- Run cache:
  - acct.take() runs on every sender change, because the tuple is built before matching (:10146), so a run never reuses the previous sender's balance.
  - BalanceCache::load caches on success and caches nothing on an error (:346-364), so a later read hits the cache.
  - set marks dirty and pushes to the dirty list once (:367-386). No other sender's set can fall inside a run, so one set per run that granted leaves the same rows, flags and even the same unsorted dirty list.
  - The balance loads lazily at the run's first extra > 0, so the backend reads and the reader-fault calls are the same. note_reader_fault (:1705) keeps only the first local fault.
- Arithmetic: the grant uses the same expression per candidate. FixedPoint Add and AddAssign both use checked_add().expect() (torus-types/src/lib.rs:235-262), and reserved + grant <= target cannot overflow.
- Panics and failures: there is no new release-build panic; both asserts are debug_assert, compiled out because there is no profile override. A Phase-2 worker panic falls back to the serial loop before the list exists (:7601-7615). Read faults still fail-stop through reader_fault exactly as before.

result.summary:
Audit 1 of exp/archy-s58-parallel-classic-book-save @8525822b (one commit on exp/archy-s58-perf-search = a44000e0), read-only. Result: OK to merge, no blocking issues.

1. Flag unset is identical to main.
- The new middle arm (native_executor.rs:6706) runs only in Classic. Its gate returns false before it looks at any book, so the exec pool is never touched (6829-6833).
- The flag read (2756-2771) costs one thread-local read and one OnceLock load per block. The only visible difference is a single info log line the first time it is read.
- The serial Classic loop (6715-6742) is unchanged. The diff outside the new code is two doc-comment edits (around 5161 and 5212).

2. Flag set gives the same state on every node and every run.
- The bytes equal `borsh::to_vec` by construction. In borsh 1.6.1, `to_vec` is `with_capacity(1024)` plus the same serialize call (helpers.rs:13-20). `encode_classic_book_into` (2790-2798) makes that same call.
- The Order, OrderBook and StopOrder encoders only read fields: BTreeMap, VecDeque and Vec in order, Address bytes, i128 and u128 big-endian (order_book.rs:4309-4352, 4446+, 4577-4620; position.rs:21-33). No interned handles, thread-locals or floats.
- The journal discards only clear the book's own containers (order_book.rs:3950-3962).
- `run_jobs` returns results in job order and catches each job's panic (exec_pool.rs:43-58). The ids are collected in the same heaviest-first order as the jobs, then re-sorted ascending before the puts (6866-6911). Both sort keys are unique.
- Puts stay serial and ascending. Put errors use today's latch text, and encode errors are logged and skipped as today (6915-6932). Encode errors cannot actually happen with a Vec writer.
- A job panic latches "book save: encode job panicked (market X): msg" (6933-6943). `latch_save_fault` keeps the first fault (4216-4220).
- That latch fail-stops at app.rs:3992-4003: exec_failed is set, nothing is flushed and the resident books are not stashed. Pool threads are outside the R01b fail-stop list (main.rs:1803-1809), so this latch is the fail-stop route.
- Release builds unwind on panic (no `panic = "abort"` anywhere), so catch_unwind is live. The overlay stores the Vec as-is and never looks at its capacity (backend.rs:2479-2490). `save_order_books_deferred` returns None for Classic (7078-7080).

3. Consensus is unaffected.
- The bytes are the same whether a node has the flag or not, so mixed-flag validators agree.
- It is fork-join on the exec thread; the borrow checker enforces that jobs end before the puts.
- The only other `run_jobs` callers are match and settle pass A (market_workers.rs:183, native_executor.rs:9288), both fork-join. No sibling s58 branch adds a background user of the pool or touches exec_pool.rs.

4. Tests are adequate.
- 11 inline tests and 3 integration tests compare the serial and parallel paths on: put sequence, rows, counter and marker rows, post-save books and journals, roots, the full-scan oracle, cold reload, a flag alternating per block, and injected put faults. They assert that the parallel path actually ran on at least 25 of 30 blocks.
- Wrong id/result alignment, descending puts, a missing discard, an off-by-one gate and panic-to-skip would all fail.
- I checked the logs in /tmp/claude-1000/s58-pcbs: green1 14/14, env-on 60/60, rdeps-on 1973/1973, ws 3826/3826. The mutation snapshot differs from HEAD only by rustfmt reflow and doc text.

5. It matches the spec.
- All three measured costs (serialize, realloc, journal discard) move off the exec thread, and the presize removes the realloc. Bench orders carry no client order id (bench-throughput main.rs:380/756/1356), so the 97 B per order hint is exact.
- No dead or debug code: the planted faults are `cfg(test)` only. The plan doc docs/plans/exp-archy-s58-parallel-classic-book-save.md is present. The 300-book microbench gate passes.

6. Codex: /tmp/claude-1000/codex-s58-parallel-classic-book-save.md says no actionable regressions, so nothing needed handling.

On your question about the paused runs:
- This experiment had nothing paused. Its reflog shows the branch created from exp/archy-s58-perf-search at 17:44:45 and one commit at 18:43:04, and no other ref exists for it.
- The paused work is the four s123 branches, checked live. All sit on c612dc7f, 1-2 commits ahead and 29 behind a44000e0:

The test plants only one panic (the planted-fault slot holds one market) and pre-sets fatal_error. So it tests that the first latched fault wins, not the order between a panic and a later fault. Rename it, or add a case with a panic on a low market and a put fault on a higher one.

3. No test pins "flag unset never calls exec_pool::pool()". That rests on code inspection of 6830-6832; a test is optional.

   - The plan itself says each worker runs about 3-4x slower than alone. That puts the parallel encode's total CPU at roughly 2-3x the serial 22 ms, about +25-45 ms CPU per block per node at 600 s.

I re-checked the reference points in section 67.3. The n=4 CI is about ±1.3% at 300m and ±1.0% at 10m. The measured trade-off there was +3.0% matched/s for -10.2% block_ms, about 0.3% per 1% of block_ms. Most single-arm claims assume 0.8 to 1.0 per 1%.
